Corollary 1.39Desingularization of a corner

Let \(\alpha \in (\frac74,2)\), \(0{\lt}\epsilon {\lt}\epsilon _0\), and \(F\) the solution of theorem 1.31 with \(T=0\). Then \(\widetilde{F}(x,t)=F(-x,-t)\) is a classical solution of ?? on \(\mathbb {R}\times (0,\infty )\), \(\widetilde{F}\in C^\infty \), and \(\| \widetilde{F}(\cdot ,t)-\sqrt\epsilon \, x_+\| _{L^\infty }\le C\sqrt\epsilon \, t^{1/\alpha }\to 0\) as \(t\downarrow 0\), where \(x_+=\max \{ x,0\} \).

Definition 1.10The coefficient \(A_\epsilon \)

For \(\epsilon \ge 0\) and \(u\in \mathbb {R}\) let \(A_\epsilon (u)=(1+\epsilon u^2)^{-\alpha /2}\) and \(B_\epsilon (u)=A_\epsilon (u)^{-1}=(1+\epsilon u^2)^{\alpha /2}\). Then \(A_\epsilon \) is smooth, \(0{\lt}A_\epsilon \le 1\), \(A_\epsilon (0)=1\), \(A_\epsilon '(0)=0\), \(A_0\equiv 1\), and \(|A_\epsilon '(u)|=\alpha \epsilon |u|(1+\epsilon u^2)^{-\alpha /2-1}\le \alpha \epsilon |u|\).

Definition 4.38Approximate solution family

Fix \(\delta \in (0,|\mu _*|/2]\), \(\overline{B}=\overline{B}(\mu _*,\delta )=\{ \mu \in \mathbb {C}:|\mu -\mu _*|\le \delta \} \) (so \(|\mu |\le 2|\mu _*|\)). Let \(C_\lambda \) be the constant of lemma 4.37 for \(k=0\), \(K_\mu =2|\mu _*|\), and fix \(\epsilon _0:=\min \{ 1,(2C_\lambda )^{-1}\} \) (so \(|\widetilde{\lambda }_{\epsilon ,\mu }(y)|\le \frac12\) for \(y\ge 1\); later chapters may decrease \(\epsilon _0\)). Let \(R_0:=\max \{ y_0,2\} \) with \(y_0\) from lemma 4.27, and fix \(R\ge R_0\) (in particular \(R\ge 2\); later chapters may enlarge \(R_0\)). Let \(\chi _R(y):=\chi _+(y/R)\) (so \(\chi _R=0\) on \((-\infty ,R]\), \(\chi _R=1\) on \([2R,\infty )\), \(|\partial ^j\chi _R|\le \| \chi _+^{(j)}\| _\infty R^{-j}\)). For \(\epsilon \in [0,\epsilon _0]\), \(\mu \in \overline{B}\) and \(y{\gt}R/2\) define

\begin{equation} \label{eqn:approx_modified_frequency} \lambda _{\epsilon ,\mu }(y):=\Psi _{\epsilon ,\mu }'(y)=y^{1/p}+c_{\textup{power}}\Bigl(\frac{1-p^2}p\Bigr)y^{1/p-p-1}+\frac{c_{\textup{log}}(\mu )}y,\qquad \Psi _{\epsilon ,\mu }(R)=\Psi _0(R), \end{equation}
6

\begin{equation} \label{eqn:approx_Z_definition} Z_{\epsilon ,\mu }(y)=\mu \, a_*(y)\, \lambda _{\epsilon ,\mu }(y)^{-(p+1)/2}e^{i(\Psi _{\epsilon ,\mu }(y)-\pi /4)} . \end{equation}
7

We abbreviate \(f=\overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu }\), \(Z=Z_{\epsilon ,\mu }\), \(\lambda =\lambda _{\epsilon ,\mu }\), \(\Psi =\Psi _{\epsilon ,\mu }\), and write \(Z_0:=Z_{0,\mu _*}\) (also \(\lambda _0,\Psi _0\) agree with \(\lambda _{0,\mu },\Psi _{0,\mu }\), see lemma 4.39). Define

\begin{equation} \label{eqn:approx_slow_correction} f_{\textup{slow}}(y)=c_+y^{-p}\chi _R(y)+c_-|y|^{-p}\chi _R(-y), \end{equation}
8

\begin{equation} \label{eqn:approx_oscillatory_correction} f_{\textup{osc}}(y)=-2\chi _R(y)\operatorname {Re}\int _y^\infty \Bigl(Z_{\epsilon ,\mu }(t)+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z_{\epsilon ,\mu }(t)^3-\frac\mu {\mu _*}Z_0(t)\Bigr)dt \quad (y{\gt}R),\qquad f_{\textup{osc}}(y)=0\quad (y\le R), \end{equation}
9

(absolutely convergent, see lemma 4.40) and

\begin{equation} \label{eqn:approx_family_definition} \overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu }=f_{0,\mu }+f_{\textup{slow}}+f_{\textup{osc}} . \end{equation}
10

By lemma 4.41, for \(y\ge 2R\)

\begin{equation} \label{eqn:approx_family_positive} \overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu }(y)=f_{0,\textup{low}}(y)+c_+y^{-p}-2\operatorname {Re}\int _y^\infty \bigl(Z(t)+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z(t)^3\bigr)dt, \end{equation}
11

and for \(y\le -2R\)

\begin{equation} \label{eqn:approx_family_negative} \overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu }(y)=f_0(y)+2\operatorname {Re}\Bigl[\Bigl(\frac\mu {\mu _*}-1\Bigr)f_{0,+}(y)\Bigr]+c_-|y|^{-p}. \end{equation}
12

Definition 1.4Admissible profile class

\(\mathcal A\) denotes the set of \(f\in C^1(\mathbb {R})\) such that \(f'\in L^\infty (\mathbb {R})\) and \(f'\) is locally Lipschitz. Equivalently \(f\in W^{2,\infty }_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb {R})\) with \(f'\in L^\infty (\mathbb {R})\) (taking the \(C^1\) representative). For \(f\in \mathcal A\) and \(R{\gt}0\) write \(\mathrm{Lip}_R(f')\) for the Lipschitz constant of \(f'\) on \([-R,R]\). Note that \(\mathcal A\) contains functions with linear growth, e.g. any \(f\) with \(f'(y)\to -1\) as \(y\to -\infty \); no decay of \(f\) is required.

Definition 1.1Model corner

The model corner is \(W:\mathbb {R}\to \mathbb {R}\), \(W(y)=y_-:=\max \{ -y,0\} \).

Definition 1.11The nonlinearity \(\mathcal{J}_\epsilon \)

For \(\epsilon \ge 0\) and \(f\in \mathcal A\) define, for every \(y\in \mathbb {R}\),

\[ \mathcal{J}_\epsilon (f)(y)=c_\alpha \int _\mathbb {R}\frac{f'(y)-f'(z)}{\bigl((y-z)^2+\epsilon (f(y)-f(z))^2\bigr)^{\alpha /2}}\, dz =c_\alpha \int _\mathbb {R}\frac{f'(y)-f'(z)}{|y-z|^\alpha }A_\epsilon \bigl(S_f(y,z)\bigr)\, dz . \]

(The two integrands agree for \(z\ne y\) since \((y-z)^2+\epsilon (f(y)-f(z))^2=|y-z|^2(1+\epsilon S_f(y,z)^2)\).) We write \(\mathcal{J}:=\mathcal{J}_1\). Note \(\mathcal{J}_0(f)=|D|^p\partial _yf\).

LaTeX Lean
Definition 1.23The cubic remainder \(\mathcal{Q}_\epsilon \)

For \(\epsilon \ge 0\), \(f\in \mathcal A\) and \(y\in \mathbb {R}\),

\[ \mathcal{Q}_\epsilon (f)(y)=c_\alpha \int _\mathbb {R}\frac{f'(y)-f'(z)}{|y-z|^\alpha } \Bigl(A_\epsilon \bigl(S_f(y,z)\bigr)-1\Bigr)\, dz . \]
LaTeX Lean
Definition 1.27Quasilinear residual

For \(\epsilon \ge 0\) and \(f\in \mathcal A\) let \(\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_\epsilon (f)=|D|^{\alpha -1}\partial _yf+f-yf'+\mathcal{Q}_\epsilon (f)\), i.e. \(\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_\epsilon (f)=\mathcal{L}_0(f)+\mathcal{Q}_\epsilon (f)\) with \(\mathcal{L}_0(f)=|D|^{\alpha -1}f'+f-yf'\).

Definition 1.3Secant

For \(f:\mathbb {R}\to \mathbb {R}\) and \(y\neq z\) put \(S_f(y,z)=\dfrac {f(y)-f(z)}{y-z}\). If \(f\in C^1\) we extend by \(S_f(y,y)=f'(y)\); then \(S_f(y,z)=\int _0^1 f'(z+s(y-z))\, ds\) for all \(y,z\).

Definition 2.19Approximation properties for fixed parameters

For fixed \(P\) as in definition 2.1 and real \(R,\delta ,\epsilon _0\), let \(\mathsf A(P,R,\delta ,\epsilon _0)\) denote the following conjunction. We use the explicit family \(\overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu }\) of definition 4.38 at scale \(R\) and \(\overline{B}=\{ \mu \in \mathbb {C}:|\mu -\mu _*|\le \delta \} \). First \(\mu _*\ne 0\), and every \(\overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu }\) is real and \(C^\infty \) for \(\epsilon \in [0,\epsilon _0]\), \(\mu \in \overline{B}\). The remaining properties are:

  1. \(\lim _{y\to -\infty }[\overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu }(y)+y]=0\) and \(\lim _{y\to +\infty }\overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu }(y)=0\).

  2. For every \(j\ge 0\) there is \(C_j{\gt}0\) such that for all \(\epsilon \in [0,\epsilon _0]\), \(\mu \in \overline{B}\): for \(y\ge 0\), \(|\overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu }(y)|\le C_j\langle y \rangle ^{-p}\) and \(|\partial _y^{j+1}\overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu }(y)|\le C_j\langle y \rangle ^{-\beta +j/p}\); for \(y\le 0\), \(|\partial _y^j(\overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu }(y)+y)|\le C_j\langle y \rangle ^{-p-j}\).

  3. For every admissible \(\gamma \) there is \(C_\gamma {\gt}0\) such that for all \(\epsilon \in [0,\epsilon _0]\), \(\mu \in \overline{B}\): \(\mathcal{E}_\epsilon (\overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu })\in Y_\gamma \) and

    \begin{equation} \label{eqn:fixed_point_residual_bound} \| \mathcal{E}_\epsilon (\overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu })-G_\mu \| _{Y_\gamma }\le C_\gamma \, \epsilon , \end{equation}
    1

    where \(G_\mu \) is the real Schwartz function of definition 2.13 (independent of \(\epsilon \), \(G_{\mu _*}=0\)).

  4. For every \(\epsilon \in [0,\epsilon _0]\): the map \(\mu \mapsto \overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu }\) is continuous from \(\overline{B}\) into \(C^2_{\mathrm{loc}}\), i.e. for every compact \(K\subset \mathbb {R}\), \(k\in \{ 0,1,2\} \) and \(\mu _j\to \mu \) in \(\overline{B}\), \(\sup _K|\partial ^k_y\overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu _j}-\partial ^k_y\overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu }|\to 0\); and for every admissible \(\gamma \) the map \(\mu \mapsto \mathcal{E}_\epsilon (\overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu })\) is continuous from \(\overline{B}\) into \(Y_\gamma \) (norm topology).

Definition 2.33Selection of a fixed point when one exists

For fixed parameters \(P\), \(R,\epsilon \in \mathbb {R}\), \(\mu \in \mathbb {C}\) and radius \(\rho \in \mathbb {R}\), select a function \(w\in X_{\gamma _2}\) with \(\| w\| _{X_{\gamma _2}}\le \rho \) and \(\mathcal{H}_{\epsilon ,\mu }(w)=w\) if such a function exists, and select \(w=0\) otherwise. This total choice is denoted \(w_{\epsilon ,\mu }^{\rho }\). Existence and uniqueness on the contraction ball are a separate assertion; subsequently \(w_{\epsilon ,\mu }\) abbreviates \(w_{\epsilon ,\mu }^{C_0\epsilon }\).

Definition 2.27Forcing map and fixed point map

For \(\epsilon \in [0,\epsilon _0]\), \(\mu \in \overline{B}\), an admissible \(\gamma \) and \(w\in X_\gamma \) such that \(\mathcal{N}_{\epsilon ,\overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu }}(\mathcal{U}_\epsilon ^{-1}w)\) is defined and lies in \(Y_\gamma \) (e.g. any \(w\in X_\gamma \) by theorem 2.24), define

\begin{equation} \label{eqn:fixed_point_forcing} \mathcal{G}_{\epsilon ,\mu }(w):=-\bigl[\mathcal{V}_\epsilon ^{-1}\mathcal{E}_\epsilon (\overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu })-G_\mu \bigr]-\mathcal{V}_\epsilon ^{-1}\mathcal{N}_{\epsilon ,\overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu }}(\mathcal{U}_\epsilon ^{-1}w)\ \in Y_\gamma , \end{equation}
8

and

\begin{equation} \label{eqn:fixed_point_map} \mathcal{H}_{\epsilon ,\mu }(w):=\mathcal{T}_0\Pi \, \mathcal{G}_{\epsilon ,\mu }(w)\ \in X_\gamma . \end{equation}
9

Both are given by \(\gamma \)-independent formulas, so for \(w\in X_{\gamma _2}\) the values computed in \(\gamma _2\) and in \(\gamma _1\) coincide.

Definition 3.11Nonperturbative coefficient

For real \(p,\epsilon \) define

\[ c_\epsilon =c_\alpha \int _0^1\bigl[A_\epsilon (t)-1\bigr](1-t)^{p-1}\, dt, \qquad \alpha =p+1. \]

The integral is understood as the total Bochner integral in Lean; its role in the kernel and its quantitative bound for \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\), \(0\le \epsilon \le 1\) are proved separately below.

Definition 3.3The coefficient \(B_\epsilon \) and the kernel function \(\Gamma _\epsilon \)

Let \(\epsilon \ge 0\), \(A_\epsilon (u)=(1+\epsilon u^2)^{-\alpha /2}\) (definition 1.10) and \(B_\epsilon (u):=A_\epsilon (u)^{-1}=(1+\epsilon u^2)^{\alpha /2}\). Let \(c_\alpha =\Gamma (\alpha )\sin (\pi (\alpha -1)/2)/\pi \) be the constant of definition 1.22. Define \(P_\epsilon ,\Gamma _\epsilon :\mathbb {R}^2\to \mathbb {R}\) by

\[ P_\epsilon (u,v):=\int _u^v\Bigl(1-\frac{A_\epsilon (s)}{A_\epsilon (u)}\Bigr)ds, \]

\begin{equation} \label{eq:G_epsilon} \Gamma _\epsilon (u,v):=c_\alpha \Bigl[p\int _u^v\Bigl(1-\frac{A_\epsilon (s)}{A_\epsilon (u)}\Bigr)ds+(v-u)\Bigl(1-\frac{A_\epsilon (v)}{A_\epsilon (u)}\Bigr)\Bigr] =c_\alpha \Bigl[p\, P_\epsilon (u,v)+(v-u)\Bigl(1-\frac{A_\epsilon (v)}{A_\epsilon (u)}\Bigr)\Bigr], \end{equation}
1

and

\[ \widetilde{\Gamma }_\epsilon (u,v):=-\frac{c_\alpha }{A_\epsilon (u)}\int _0^1\bigl[1+p(1-t)\bigr]A_\epsilon '\bigl(u+t(v-u)\bigr)\, dt . \]

Since \(A_\epsilon \in C^\infty (\mathbb {R})\) and \(A_\epsilon {\gt}0\), the functions \(B_\epsilon ,P_\epsilon ,\Gamma _\epsilon ,\widetilde{\Gamma }_\epsilon \) are \(C^\infty \) on their domains.

Definition 3.1Local Hölder spaces

Let \(s{\gt}0\) with \(s\notin \mathbb {N}\), and write \(s=k+\theta \) with \(k\in \mathbb {N}_0\), \(\theta \in (0,1)\). For a compact interval \(I\subset \mathbb {R}\) and \(g\in C^k(I;\mathbb {C})\) put

\[ \| g\| _{C^s(I)}:=\sum _{i=0}^k\sup _I|g^{(i)}| +\sup _{x\neq x'\in I}\frac{|g^{(k)}(x)-g^{(k)}(x')|}{|x-x'|^\theta }, \]

and \(C^s(I)=\{ g\in C^k(I):\| g\| _{C^s(I)}{\lt}\infty \} \). For an open interval \(U\), \(C^s_{\textup{loc}}(U)\) is the set of \(g\in C^k(U)\) with \(g|_I\in C^s(I)\) for every compact interval \(I\subset U\). We write \(C^s_{\textup{loc}}=C^s_{\textup{loc}}(\mathbb {R})\). For \(0{\lt}s_0{\lt}1\) every locally Lipschitz function lies in \(C^{s_0}_{\textup{loc}}\).

For \(f\in W^{2,\infty }_{\textup{loc}}(\mathbb {R})\) with \(f'\in L^\infty (\mathbb {R})\) and \(y\in \mathbb {R}\) set

\[ \mathcal{I}_\epsilon (f)(y):=\int _\mathbb {R}\frac{\Gamma _\epsilon \bigl(f'(y),S_f(y,z)\bigr)}{|y-z|^\alpha }\, dz =\int _\mathbb {R}\frac{\Gamma _\epsilon \bigl(f'(y),S_f(y,y-t)\bigr)}{|t|^\alpha }\, dt . \]

Definition 3.87Phase data for the oscillatory multiplier

For \(a:\mathbb {R}\to \mathbb {C}\), \(\Psi :\mathbb {R}\to \mathbb {R}\), \(Y\in \mathbb {R}\), put \(\lambda =\Psi '\) and

\[ \Theta _y(z)=\Psi (y+z)-\Psi (y)-\lambda (y)z,\qquad F_y(z)=\begin{cases} a(y+z)e^{i\Theta _y(z)},& y+z\in (Y/4,4Y),\\ 0,& \text{otherwise}.\end{cases} \]

For \(k_0\in \mathbb {N}\), \(C_k\in \mathbb {R}\) and real \(\Lambda ,A,c_0\), the predicate \(\mathsf H(Y,\Lambda ,A,c_0,(C_k),k_0;a,\Psi )\) means that \(a\in C^\infty (\mathbb {R})\), \(\operatorname {supp}a\subset (Y/4,4Y)\), \(\Psi \in C^\infty ((Y/4,4Y))\), and for all \(x\in (Y/4,4Y)\) and \(0\le k\le k_0\),

\[ c_0^{-1}\Lambda \le \lambda (x)\le c_0\Lambda ,\quad |\partial ^k\lambda (x)|\le C_k\Lambda Y^{-k},\quad |\partial ^ka(x)|\le C_kAY^{-k}. \]

Positivity and size restrictions on \(Y,\Lambda ,A,c_0\) are hypotheses of the lemmas using this predicate.

Definition 3.88Multiplier coefficients and remainders

\[ \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{mult},N}(y)=e^{-i\Psi (y)}|D|^p(ae^{i\Psi })(y)-\sum _{k=0}^{2N-2}B_k(y),\qquad \widetilde{\mathcal{R}}_{\mathrm{mult},2}(y)=\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{mult},2}(y) -\frac{p(p-1)}2\lambda (y)^{p-2}a''(y). \]

The finite index set consists of \((r,q)\) with \(r\in \{ 0,\ldots ,2N-1\} \), \(q=(q_1,\ldots ,q_{2N-1})\in \{ 0,\ldots ,2N-1\} ^{2N-1}\), and \(r+\sum _{j=1}^{2N-1}j q_j=2N-1\). \[ b_t(z)=z^{2N-1}a^{(r)}(y+tz)\prod _{j=1}^{2N-1}(\Theta _y^{(j)}(tz))^{q_j} \]

when \(y+tz\in (Y/4,4Y)\), and \(b_t(z)=0\) otherwise. Put

\[ \phi _t(z)=\lambda (y)z+\Theta _y(tz),\qquad I_\eta (y,t)=\int _\mathbb {R}e^{i\phi _t(z)-\eta z^2}\frac{b_t(z)}{|z|^{1+p}}\, dz, \qquad B=A\Lambda ^{q_1+\ell }Y^{-2N+1+\ell }t^{q_1}. \]

Here \(I_\eta \) is the total Bochner integral; the hypotheses ensuring convergence and estimates are imposed in the following lemmas.

Definition 5.1Standing hypotheses and notation for this chapter

Fix \(p\in (3/4,1)\), \(\alpha =1+p\), \(\beta =\frac{p+1}{2p}\) (so \(2\beta =1+\frac1p\)). Let \(c_\alpha {\gt}0\) be the constant with \(|D|^ph(y)=c_\alpha \int _\mathbb {R}\frac{h(y)-h(z)}{|y-z|^{1+p}}\, dz\) for bounded \(C^1\) functions \(h\) (definition 1.5); for complex-valued \(h\) the same formula is used, so that \(|D|^p(\operatorname {Re}h)=\operatorname {Re}|D|^ph\). For \(g\) with \(g'\) bounded and \(C^1\) put \(\mathcal{L}_0g:=|D|^pg'+g-yg'\) (this is \(\mathcal{L}_\epsilon \) of definition 2.17 at \(\epsilon =0\)).

Fix \(\delta \in (0,|\mu _*|/2]\), \(\mu _*=-i/\sqrt{2\pi p}\) (definition 4.15), and \(\epsilon _0\in (0,\epsilon _0^*(\delta )]\), where \(\epsilon _0^*(\delta )\in (0,1]\) is the minimum of the smallness thresholds for \(\epsilon \) provided (for this \(\delta \)) by lemma 4.42, lemma 4.40, lemma 4.45, lemma 4.46, lemma 4.62, lemma 4.47, lemma 4.44 and lemma 4.48 (Lean: c05_eps0_star); put \(\overline{B}=\overline{B}(\mu _*,\delta )\), the cutoff \(\chi _+\) and the profile of \(\chi _R\) as in definition 4.38. For every \(Y{\gt}0\) let \(\chi _Y\in C^\infty (\mathbb {R};[0,1])\) be the cutoff of definition 4.51: \(\operatorname {supp}\chi _Y\subset (Y/4,4Y)\), \(\chi _Y\equiv 1\) on \([Y/2,3Y]\). We assume constants \(K_j\) (\(j\ge 0\)), independent of \(R,Y\), with \(|\partial ^j\chi _R|\le K_jR^{-j}\) and \(|\partial ^j\chi _Y|\le K_jY^{-j}\).

A parameter tuple is \((\epsilon ,\mu ,R,Y)\) with \(\epsilon \in [0,\epsilon _0]\), \(\mu \in \overline{B}\), \(R\ge R_0\), \(Y\ge 8R\), where \(R_0\ge 1\) depends only on \((p,\epsilon _0,\delta ,\chi _+)\) and is so large that for all \(y\ge R_0\): (R1) the bounds of lemma 4.33(1) hold and \(|a_*(y)-1|\le \frac12\); (R2) writing \(\lambda =\lambda _{\epsilon ,\mu }=y^{1/p}(1+\widetilde{\lambda })\) with \(\widetilde{\lambda }(y)=-\frac{c_\epsilon }{p}y^{-p-1}+c_{\textup{log}}(\mu )y^{-1-1/p}\) one has \(|\widetilde{\lambda }(y)|\le \frac12\); (R3) the estimates of lemma 4.48 hold on \([R,\infty )\).

Notation (all for \(y\ge R\)): \(Z=Z_{\epsilon ,\mu }\), \(\lambda =\lambda _{\epsilon ,\mu }\), \(\Psi =\Psi _{\epsilon ,\mu }\), \(\Phi :=\Psi -\pi /4\), \(A:=\mu a_*\lambda ^{-(p+1)/2}\), so \(Z=Ae^{i\Phi }\); \(\lambda _0=y^{1/p}\), \(\Psi _0\), \(\Phi _0:=\Psi _0-\pi /4\), \(A_0:=\mu a_*\lambda _0^{-(p+1)/2}\), so \(\frac{\mu }{\mu _*}Z_0=A_0e^{i\Phi _0}\). The constants \(c_\epsilon ,n_\epsilon ,c_{\textup{cubic}},c_{\textup{log}}(\mu )\), the cubic operator \(\mathcal{Q}_{\epsilon ,3}\), the function \(f_{\textup{osc}}\), the local front \(v_Y\) and \(\mathcal{E}_5\) are those of ??; in particular \(\mathcal{Q}_{\epsilon ,3}(2\sin )(x)=2n_\epsilon \cos x-2(3^p-1)c_{\textup{cubic}}\cos (3x)\) and \(v_Y(z)=-2\chi _Y(z)\operatorname {Re}\int _z^\infty (Z+c_{\textup{cubic}}Z^3)\, dt\).

An admissible constant is a number \(C\in (0,\infty )\) depending only on \(p,c_\alpha ,\epsilon _0,\delta ,\chi _+,(K_j)_j\) (and, where indicated, on an integer \(k\)), but not on the tuple \((\epsilon ,\mu ,R,Y)\) nor on the points \(y,s,t,z\).

Definition 7.1Free operator, cubic remainder, divided residual

Let \(f\in C^2(\mathbb {R};\mathbb {R})\) with \(f'\in L^\infty (\mathbb {R})\) and \(0\le \epsilon \le 1\).

  1. The secant is \(S_f(y,z):=\frac{f(y)-f(z)}{y-z}\) for \(y\neq z\).

  2. The free operator is \(\mathcal{L}_0(f):=|D|^pf'+f-yf'\) (this is \(\mathcal{L}_\epsilon \) of definition 2.17 at \(\epsilon =0\)).

  3. The nonlinear remainder is \(\mathcal{Q}_\epsilon (f)(y):=c_\alpha \int _\mathbb {R}\frac{f'(y)-f'(z)}{|y-z|^\alpha }\bigl[A_\epsilon (S_f(y,z))-1\bigr]\, dz\).

  4. The divided residual is \(\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_\epsilon (f):=A_\epsilon (f')\, \mathcal{E}_\epsilon (f)\), where \(\mathcal{E}_\epsilon \) is the residual of definition 1.26.

  5. The corner profile is \(W(y):=\max \{ -y,0\} \).

LaTeX Lean
Definition 7.2Secant kernel operator

For \(f\in C^2(\mathbb {R};\mathbb {R})\) with \(f'\) bounded and \(\Gamma \in C^1(\mathbb {R};\mathbb {R})\), set

\[ \mathcal{T}_\Gamma (f)(y):=c_\alpha \int _\mathbb {R}\frac{f'(y)-f'(y-s)}{|s|^\alpha }\, \Gamma \bigl(S_f(y,y-s)\bigr)\, ds, \qquad S_f(y,y-s)=\frac{f(y)-f(y-s)}{s}. \]

Thus \(\mathcal{T}_1(f)=|D|^pf'\), \(\mathcal{T}_{A_\epsilon -1}(f)=\mathcal{Q}_\epsilon (f)\) and, by linearity in \(\Gamma \), \(\mathcal{T}_{A_\epsilon }(f)=|D|^pf'+\mathcal{Q}_\epsilon (f)\) (whenever the integrals converge absolutely, see lemma 7.7). For \(K{\gt}0\) write \(\| \Gamma \| _{K}:=\sup _{|u|\le K}(|\Gamma (u)|+|\Gamma '(u)|)\).

Definition 7.3Admissible profile class

For \(K\geq 1\), \(\mathcal{P}(K)\) is the set of \(f\in C^3(\mathbb {R};\mathbb {R})\) such that for all \(y\in \mathbb {R}\):

  1. \(|f'(y)|\le K\);

  2. \(|f''(y)|\le K\langle y \rangle ^{\theta }\) if \(y\geq 0\), and \(|f''(y)|\le K\langle y \rangle ^{-1}\) if \(y\le 0\) (recall \(\theta =\tfrac 1p-\beta \));

  3. \(|f'''(y)|\le K\langle y \rangle ^{2/p}\).

\begin{equation} \label{eqn:linear_frequency_split} \widehat{\mathcal{T}_{\rm l}G}:=\chi \, m_G,\qquad \widehat{\mathcal{T}_{\rm h}G}:=(1-\chi )\, m_G, \end{equation}

i.e. \(\mathcal{T}_{\rm l}G(y)=\frac1{2\pi }\int \chi (\xi )m_G(\xi )e^{iy\xi }d\xi \) (a bounded \(C^\infty \) real function, as \(\chi m_G\) is bounded, compactly supported and Hermitian), and \(\mathcal{T}_{\rm h}G=\check{((1-\chi )m_G)}\in \mathcal S'\). In Lean, the high-frequency operator is the continuous, polynomially bounded real representative with this transform when one exists, and is \(0\) otherwise, as for \(\mathcal{T}_0\) in definition 8.33. Membership in \(X_\gamma \) alone therefore does not establish its Fourier transform; the reconstruction statement and its norm bound are recorded separately in lemma 8.59.

Definition 8.2The conjugating diffeomorphism

Let \(c\in \mathbb {R}\) with \(|c|\le \frac12\). Define \(b_c:\mathbb {R}\to \mathbb {R}\) by \(b_c(y)=c\, \chi _+(y)y^{-p}\) for \(y{\gt}1\) and \(b_c(y)=0\) for \(y\le 1\) (so \(b_c\in C^\infty (\mathbb {R})\) since \(\chi _+=0\) on \((-\infty ,1]\), and \(|b_c(y)|\le |c|\)). Since \(t-b_c(t)\ge t-\frac12{\gt}0\) for \(t\ge 1\), we may define

\[ \phi _c(y):=y\quad (y\le 1),\qquad \phi _c(y):=\Bigl[1+\frac{p+1}{p}\int _1^y\bigl(t-b_c(t)\bigr)^{1/p}dt\Bigr]^{\frac p{p+1}}\quad (y{\gt}1). \]

Put \(\psi _c:=\phi _c^{-1}\) (a bijection of \(\mathbb {R}\) by lemma 8.4). For \(\epsilon \ge 0\) with \(|c_\epsilon |\le \frac12\) we write \(\phi _\epsilon :=\phi _{c_\epsilon }\), \(\psi _\epsilon :=\psi _{c_\epsilon }\), and \(b_\epsilon =b_{c_\epsilon }\) (which is the coefficient of definition 2.17).

Definition 10.16A dominated pair of value and derivative kernels

Let \(1{\lt}\alpha {\lt}2\), let \(U\subset \mathbb {R}\) be a nonempty open interval, and let \(A\ge 0\). For \(s\ne 0\) put

\[ \omega _0(s)=\frac{\min \{ |s|^2,1\} }{|s|^\alpha },\qquad \omega _1(s)=\frac{\min \{ |s|,1\} }{|s|^\alpha }, \]

and put \(\omega _0(0)=\omega _1(0)=0\). A pair of Borel measurable functions \(H,J:\mathbb {R}^2\to \mathbb {R}\) is a dominated kernel pair on \(U\) with constant \(A\) if:

  1. \(H(y,y)=J(y,y)=0\) for every \(y\in U\);

  2. for each fixed \(z\), \(H(\cdot ,z)\) is locally Lipschitz on \(U\setminus \{ z\} \) and \(\partial _y H(y,z)=J(y,z)\) for a.e. \(y\in U\setminus \{ z\} \);

  3. \(|H(y,z)|\le A\omega _0(y-z)\) for all \(y\in U\) and \(z\ne y\);

  4. there is a null set \(E\subset U\) such that \(|J(y,z)|\le A\omega _1(y-z)\) for every \(y\in U\setminus E\) and every \(z\ne y\).

Here local Lipschitz regularity is for the actual pointwise representative, and the null set in (4) is independent of \(z\).

Definition 10.1The three nonlinear pieces

Let \(0\le \epsilon \le 1\), let \(\overline{f}\in C^2(\mathbb {R})\) with \(\overline{f}'\in L^\infty (\mathbb {R})\), and let \(r\in X_\gamma \) (for some \(\gamma {\gt}1/p\), so that \(r'\in L^\infty \)). Definition 11.1Fixed cutoffs and dyadic operators

Use the even cutoff \(\chi =\rho \) of definition 4.4. Set

Let \(K_p=\operatorname {Re}\check{q_p}\) and \(K_{p,j}(x)=2^{(1-p)j}K_p(2^jx)\) for \(j\in \mathbb {N}\). For a real function \(v\) put

Definition 12.14Admissible graphs, patches and canonical representatives

Let \(I\) be a nonempty open time interval. A graph \(F:\mathbb {R}\times I\to \mathbb {R}\) is admissible if it is jointly smooth on \(\mathbb {R}\times I\) (no smoothness is required at the endpoints of \(I\) or outside \(\mathbb {R}\times I\)) and for every compact interval \(J_0\subset I\) there is \(M_{J_0}\ge 0\) with \(|F_x(x,t)|\le M_{J_0}\) for all \(x\in \mathbb {R},t\in J_0\). No global bound on \(F\), \(F_{xx}\) or time derivatives at spatial infinity is assumed. Put \(\gamma _t(s)=(s,F(s,t))\), \(\tau _t(s)=(1,F_x(s,t))\), \(\Omega _t=\{ (x,y):y{\lt}F(x,t)\} \), and \(\theta _F=\mathbf1_{\Omega _t}\). Define, for \(X\notin \Gamma _t=\gamma _t(\mathbb {R})\),

\[ U_{\alpha ,c}[F](X,t)=-c\int _\mathbb {R}\tau _t(s)|X-\gamma _t(s)|^{-\alpha }ds, \]

and give \(U\) value zero on \(\Gamma _t\). This candidate boundary representation is not assumed to satisfy the two-dimensional velocity law; that is proved in section 12.4. Define separately

\[ W_{\alpha ,c}[F](x,t)=c\int _\mathbb {R}[F_x(x,t)-F_x(s,t)]|\gamma _t(x)-\gamma _t(s)|^{-\alpha }ds. \]

The graph normal is \((-F_x,1)/\sqrt{1+F_x^2}\); \(W\) is its normal velocity multiplied by \(\sqrt{1+F_x^2}\). It is not the value of the arbitrarily extended vector field on the graph.

Definition 12.1Kernel, adjoint cancellation and renormalized potential

Let \(E=\mathbb {R}^2\) with the Euclidean norm, and write \((x,y)\in E\) for the point with coordinates \(x,y\). For a vector field \(Q:E\to E\) put \(\operatorname {div}Q=\partial _1Q_1+\partial _2Q_2\). For \(z\ne 0\) set

\[ P_{\alpha ,c}(z)=c|z|^{-\alpha },\qquad K_{\alpha ,c}(z)=\alpha c\, Jz\, |z|^{-\alpha -2}=-J\nabla P_{\alpha ,c}(z), \]

and set both kernels to zero at the single point zero. For a vector test function \(\Phi :E\to E\) define

\[ B^*_{\alpha ,c}\Phi (Y)=\int _E K_{\alpha ,c}(z)\cdot (\Phi (Y+z)-\Phi (Y))\, dz. \]

For a bounded measurable real density \(\theta \) define

\[ V_{\alpha ,c}[\theta ](X)=\int _E [P_{\alpha ,c}(X-Y)-\mathbf1_{|Y|{\gt}1}P_{\alpha ,c}(-Y)]\theta (Y)\, dY. \]

These are total formulas; the next lemmas establish their analytic meanings. The unsubtracted integral \(P*\theta \) is not asserted to converge for an infinite patch.

Definition 12.2Canonical and front normalizations

Put

\[ A_\alpha =\frac{2^{2-\alpha }\pi \Gamma (1-\alpha /2)}{\Gamma (\alpha /2)},\qquad c_{\rm std}=A_\alpha ^{-1},\qquad c_{\rm front}=\operatorname {calpha}(\alpha -1),\qquad \kappa _\alpha =\frac{c_{\rm front}}{c_{\rm std}}. \]

The two-dimensional Fourier convention is \(\widehat f(\xi )=\int _E f(X)e^{-iX\cdot \xi }dX\), with inverse factor \((2\pi )^{-2}\). The canonical operator \(-\nabla ^\perp (-\Delta )^{-1+\alpha /2}\) has multiplier \(-iJ\xi |\xi |^{\alpha -2}\), given value zero at \(\xi =0\). Identification of the real-space operator with this multiplier is a theorem below. The two coefficients are kept distinct; the final application records the corresponding time change.

Definition 12.27Weak patch system with coefficient \(c\)

A scalar (respectively vector) spacetime test on \(E\times I\) is a smooth compactly supported function \(E\times \mathbb {R}\to \mathbb {R}\) (respectively \(E\times \mathbb {R}\to E\)) whose support lies in \(E\times I\). A bounded measurable density \(\theta :E\times I\to \mathbb {R}\) and a measurable \(u\in L^1_{\rm loc}(E\times I;E)\) obey the coefficient-\(c\) velocity law if, for every vector spacetime test \(\Phi \),

\[ \int _I\! \int _E u(X,t)\cdot \Phi (X,t)dXdt =\int _I\! \int _E\theta (Y,t)B^*_{\alpha ,c}(\Phi (\cdot ,t))(Y)dYdt. \]

They solve the weak patch system if also, for every scalar spacetime test \(\zeta \),

\[ \int _I\! \int _E\theta (X,t) [\partial _t\zeta (X,t)+u(X,t)\cdot \nabla _X\zeta (X,t)]dXdt=0. \]

All pairings must be absolutely integrable. For \(\theta =\theta _F\) boundedness is automatic. With \(c=c_{\rm std}\) this is the canonical gSQG operator, as identified in section 12.1. The product \(\theta u\) is formed only after obtaining the locally integrable velocity representative.

Let \(\gamma {\gt}1\) (so \(Y_\gamma \subset L^1(\mathbb {R})\) and \(\widehat G\) is a bounded continuous function, with the Fourier transform of definition 1.2). For \(G\in Y_\gamma \) define

whenever the limit exists. \(\ell \) is \(\mathbb {R}\)-linear (not \(\mathbb {C}\)-linear: \(Y_\gamma \) is a real space). For admissible \(\gamma \) put \(\widetilde{Y}_\gamma :=\{ G\in Y_\gamma :\ell (G)=0\} \).

Definition 1.2Fourier transform

For \(f\in L^1(\mathbb {R};\mathbb {C})\) the Fourier transform is

\[ \widehat f(\xi )=\int _{-\infty }^{\infty } f(x)e^{-ix\xi }\, dx ,\qquad \xi \in \mathbb {R}, \]

extended to tempered distributions \(\mathcal S'(\mathbb {R})\) by duality, \(\langle \widehat u,\varphi \rangle =\langle u,\widehat\varphi \rangle \). The inverse transform is \(\check{g}(x)=\frac1{2\pi }\int _\mathbb {R}g(\xi )e^{ix\xi }\, d\xi \). With this convention \(\widehat{\partial _x f}(\xi )=i\xi \widehat f(\xi )\). A Fourier multiplier with symbol \(m\in L^\infty _{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb {R})\) of polynomial growth acts on \(f\in \mathcal S(\mathbb {R})\) by \(m(D)f=(m\widehat f)^{\vee }\). (Mathlib’s Real.fourierIntegral uses \(e^{-2\pi i x\xi }\); the two conventions differ by the substitution \(\xi \mapsto 2\pi \xi \).)

Definition 1.5The fractional multiplier \(|D|^{p}\) and \(|D|^{p}\partial _y\)

Let \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\), \(\alpha =p+1\).

  1. For \(g\in L^\infty (\mathbb {R})\) which is locally Lipschitz, define pointwise for every \(y\in \mathbb {R}\)

    \[ |D|^{p}g(y):=c_\alpha \int _\mathbb {R}\frac{g(y)-g(z)}{|y-z|^{\alpha }}\, dz . \]

    (The integral is absolutely convergent by lemma 1.6; no principal value is needed because \(\alpha {\lt}2\).)

  2. For \(f\in \mathcal A\) define \(|D|^{p}\partial _y f:=|D|^p(f')\), i.e.

    \[ |D|^{\alpha -1}\partial _y f(y)=c_\alpha \int _\mathbb {R}\frac{f'(y)-f'(z)}{|y-z|^{\alpha }}\, dz . \]

    This is the meaning of \(|D|^{\alpha -1}\partial _y f\) for non-decaying \(f\) (e.g. \(f'\to -1\) at \(-\infty \)): only \(f'\) enters, and \(f'\) is bounded.

  3. (Fourier side.) For \(f\in \mathcal S(\mathbb {R})\), \(|D|^p f=(|\xi |^{p}\widehat f)^\vee \) and \(|D|^{p}\partial _y f=(i\xi |\xi |^{p}\widehat f)^\vee \); the two definitions agree on \(\mathcal S(\mathbb {R})\) by lemma 1.8.

Definition 1.13Front equation; classical solution

Let \(I\subset \mathbb {R}\) be an open interval. A function \(F:\mathbb {R}\times I\to \mathbb {R}\) is a classical solution of the gSQG front equation

\begin{equation} \label{eqn:front_equation} \partial _tF(x,t)=c_\alpha \int _\mathbb {R}\frac{\partial _xF(x,t)-\partial _xF(x',t)}{\bigl((x-x')^2+(F(x,t)-F(x',t))^2\bigr)^{\alpha /2}}\, dx' \end{equation}
1

on \(\mathbb {R}\times I\) if

  1. \(F\in C^1(\mathbb {R}\times I)\), \(F(\cdot ,t)\in C^2(\mathbb {R})\) for every \(t\in I\), and \(\partial _x^2F\) is continuous on \(\mathbb {R}\times I\);

  2. for every \(t\in I\), \(\partial _xF(\cdot ,t)\in L^\infty (\mathbb {R})\) (hence \(F(\cdot ,t)\in \mathcal A\));

  3. for every \((x,t)\in \mathbb {R}\times I\), \(\partial _tF(x,t)=\mathcal{J}(F(\cdot ,t))(x)\), the right side being the absolutely convergent integral of lemma 1.12.

This is the graph (front) formulation of the gSQG patch problem with \(\Omega (t)=\{ x_2{\lt}F(x_1,t)\} \); we take ?? as the definition and do not formalize its derivation from the gSQG system.

Definition 1.22The lower-order nonlinearity \(\widetilde{\mathcal{J}}_\epsilon \)

For \(\epsilon \ge 0\), \(f\in \mathcal A\) and \(y\in \mathbb {R}\),

\[ \widetilde{\mathcal{J}}_\epsilon (f)(y)=c_\alpha \int _\mathbb {R}\frac{f'(y)-f'(z)}{|y-z|^\alpha } \Bigl(A_\epsilon \bigl(S_f(y,z)\bigr)-A_\epsilon \bigl(f'(y)\bigr)\Bigr)\, dz . \]
LaTeX Lean
Definition 2.17Linear operators \(\mathcal{L}_0\), \(\mathcal{L}_\epsilon \)

For \(r\in X_\gamma \) (\(\gamma \) admissible) define the function \(\mathcal{L}_0 r:\mathbb {R}\to \mathbb {R}\) by

\[ \mathcal{L}_0r:=|D|^p\partial _yr+r-y\, \partial _yr, \]

where \(|D|^p\partial _y\) is as in definition 1.5. For admissible \(\gamma \), \(r'\) is bounded, integrable and locally Lipschitz; its derivative need not be globally bounded. For \(\epsilon \ge 0\) let \(b_\epsilon (y):=c_\epsilon \chi _+(y)y^{-p}\) with \(c_\epsilon \) defined in definition 3.11 (\(b_\epsilon :=0\) for \(y\le 1\)), and define

\[ \mathcal{L}_\epsilon r:=\mathcal{L}_0r+b_\epsilon \, \partial _yr+\mathcal{R}_\epsilon r, \]

where \(\mathcal{R}_\epsilon \) is the remainder operator of definition 8.9. In general \(\mathcal{L}_\epsilon r\notin Y_\gamma \) (the term \(y\, r'\) grows like \(\langle y \rangle ^{1+1/p-\gamma }\) relative to the \(Y_\gamma \) weight); \(\mathcal{L}_\epsilon \) is only a linear map from \(X_\gamma \) into functions \(\mathbb {R}\to \mathbb {R}\).

\(\mu _*:=-\dfrac {i}{\sqrt{2\pi p}}\in \mathbb {C}\setminus \{ 0\} \).

LaTeX Lean
Definition 2.18Nonlinear operator \(\mathcal{N}_{\epsilon ,\overline{f}}\)

For \(\epsilon \ge 0\), a profile \(\overline{f}\) for which \(\mathcal{E}_\epsilon (\overline{f})\) is defined (definition 1.26), and \(r\in X_\gamma \) such that \(\mathcal{E}_\epsilon (\overline{f}+r)\) is defined, set

\[ \mathcal{N}_{\epsilon ,\overline{f}}(r):=\mathcal{E}_\epsilon (\overline{f}+r)-\mathcal{E}_\epsilon (\overline{f})-\mathcal{L}_\epsilon (r), \]

so that \(\mathcal{E}_\epsilon (\overline{f}+r)=\mathcal{E}_\epsilon (\overline{f})+\mathcal{L}_\epsilon (r)+\mathcal{N}_{\epsilon ,\overline{f}}(r)\) identically.

Definition 10.4Admissible profile

Let \(M{\gt}0\). A function \(\overline{f}\in C^2(\mathbb {R};\mathbb {R})\) is an admissible profile with constant \(M\) if for all \(y\ge 0\)

\[ |\overline{f}(y)|\le M\langle y \rangle ^{-p},\qquad |\overline{f}'(y)|\le M\langle y \rangle ^{-\beta },\qquad |\overline{f}''(y)|\le M\langle y \rangle ^{-\beta +1/p}, \]

and for all \(y\le 0\)

\[ |\overline{f}(y)+y|\le M\langle y \rangle ^{-p},\qquad |\overline{f}'(y)+1|\le M\langle y \rangle ^{-p-1},\qquad |\overline{f}''(y)|\le M\langle y \rangle ^{-p-2}. \]
LaTeX Lean
Definition 2.1Fixed parameters and cutoff

Fix once and for all real numbers \(p,\alpha ,\beta ,\gamma _1,\gamma _2\) with

\[ \frac34 {\lt} p {\lt} 1,\qquad \alpha = p+1,\qquad \beta = \frac{p+1}{2p},\qquad \beta +\frac1p {\lt} \gamma _1 {\lt} \gamma _2 {\lt} 2p+1 . \]

(Thus \(\alpha \in (\tfrac 74,2)\).) We call \(\gamma \) admissible if \(\beta +\frac1p{\lt}\gamma {\lt}2p+1\); both \(\gamma _1\) and \(\gamma _2\) are admissible. Fix also a cutoff \(\chi _+\in C^\infty (\mathbb {R};[0,1])\), nondecreasing, with \(\chi _+(\xi )=0\) for \(\xi \le 1\) and \(\chi _+(\xi )=1\) for \(\xi \ge 2\); in particular \(\chi _+'\in C^\infty _c(\mathbb {R})\), \(\operatorname {supp}\chi _+'\subset [1,2]\) and \(\int _0^\infty \chi _+'(\xi )\, d\xi =1\). (The same function \(\chi _+\) is used as a cutoff in the variable \(y\) elsewhere.) Finally let \(\Phi _0(\xi ):=\frac1\alpha \, \xi |\xi |^{p}\) for \(\xi \in \mathbb {R}\).

Definition 2.15The projection \(\Pi \)

For admissible \(\gamma \) and \(G\in Y_\gamma \) define

\[ \Pi G:=G-\operatorname {Re}(\ell (G))\, G_+-\operatorname {Im}(\ell (G))\, G_- . \]

(\(\Pi \) is given by the same formula for every \(\gamma \), so \(\Pi \) on \(Y_{\gamma _2}\) is the restriction of \(\Pi \) on \(Y_{\gamma _1}\).)

Definition 1.29Profile equation

Let \(\epsilon \ge 0\). A function \(f\in \mathcal A\) solves the self-similar profile equation if

\begin{equation} \label{eqn:main_ideas_self_similar_front_equation_semilinear} |D|^{\alpha -1}\partial _yf+\frac{1}{A_\epsilon (\partial _yf)}\Bigl(f-y\partial _yf+\widetilde{\mathcal{J}}_\epsilon (f)\Bigr)=0 \quad \text{i.e. }\ \mathcal{E}_\epsilon (f)(y)=0\ \ \forall y\in \mathbb {R}, \end{equation}
4

together with the boundary conditions \(\lim _{y\to -\infty }f'(y)=-1\) and \(\lim _{y\to +\infty }f(y)=0\). (The boundary conditions are not used in the reduction lemma 1.30; they encode that \(F\) approaches the corner \(\sqrt\epsilon \, x_-\).)

Definition 8.9Remainder \(\mathcal{R}_\epsilon \)

For \(y\neq z\) let

\[ K_\epsilon (y,z):=c_\alpha \Bigl[1-\Bigl(\frac{\phi _\epsilon '(y)}{S_{\phi _\epsilon }(y,z)}\Bigr)^{p+1}\Bigr]\frac1{|y-z|^{1+p}} . \]

For \(r\in C^1(\mathbb {R})\) with \(r'\) bounded define

\begin{equation} \label{eqn:linear_R1} \mathcal{R}_{1,\epsilon }r:=\bigl((\phi _\epsilon ')^{p+1}-1\bigr)r, \end{equation}
5

\begin{equation} \label{eqn:linear_R2} \mathcal{R}_{2,\epsilon }r(y):=\int _\mathbb {R}K_\epsilon (y,z)\, r'(z)\, dz =c_\alpha \int _\mathbb {R}\Bigl[1-\Bigl(\frac{\phi _\epsilon '(y)}{S_{\phi _\epsilon }(y,z)}\Bigr)^{p+1}\Bigr]\frac{r'(z)}{|y-z|^{1+p}}\, dz, \end{equation}
6

(absolutely convergent by ??) and \(\mathcal{R}_\epsilon :=\mathcal{R}_{1,\epsilon }+\mathcal{R}_{2,\epsilon }\). For \(\epsilon =0\) (\(c_0=0\), \(\phi _0=\mathrm{id}\)) one has \(\mathcal{R}_0=0\).

\[ D\mathcal{Q}_\epsilon (W)[h](y):=c_\alpha \int _{-\infty }^0\Bigl[(h'(y)-h'(z))\Bigl(A_\epsilon \Bigl(\frac z{y-z}\Bigr)-1\Bigr)+A_\epsilon '\Bigl(\frac z{y-z}\Bigr)S_h(y,z)\Bigr]\frac{dz}{(y-z)^\alpha }, \]

absolutely convergent (\(|h'|,|S_h|\le \| h'\| _\infty \), \((y-z)^{-\alpha }\in L^1(-\infty ,0)\)). With \(f=\overline{f}_{\epsilon ,\mu }\), for \(y{\gt}R\) set

Definition 1.17Self-similar ansatz

For \(T\in \mathbb {R}\) let \(L_T(t)=(\alpha (T-t))^{1/\alpha }\) for \(t{\lt}T\). For \(\epsilon {\gt}0\) and \(f:\mathbb {R}\to \mathbb {R}\) define \(F=F_{\epsilon ,T,f}:\mathbb {R}\times (-\infty ,T)\to \mathbb {R}\) by

\begin{equation} \label{eqn:intro_self_similar_ansatz} F(x,t)=\sqrt\epsilon \, L_T(t)\, f\Bigl(\frac{x}{L_T(t)}\Bigr). \end{equation}
2

We call \(y=x/L_T(t)\) the self-similar variable and \(f\) the profile. The self-similar time is \(\tau =-\log L_T(t)\).

Definition 8.33The free inverse \(\mathcal{T}_0\) and the subspace \(\widetilde{Y}_\gamma \)

For \(\gamma {\gt}1\) and \(G\in Y_\gamma \) (so \(G\in L^1\) and \(\widehat G\) is bounded and continuous) define \(m_G:\mathbb {R}\to \mathbb {C}\),

\begin{equation} \label{eqn:linear_free_inverse} m_G(\xi ):=\int _0^1t\, e^{-i(1-t^{p+1})\Phi _0(\xi )}\, \widehat G(t\xi )\, dt \; =\; \frac{e^{-i\Phi _0(\xi )}}{\xi ^2}\int _0^\xi \eta \, e^{i\Phi _0(\eta )}\widehat G(\eta )\, d\eta \quad (\xi \neq 0), \end{equation}
11

(for \(\xi {\lt}0\), \(\int _0^\xi \) is the oriented integral) and \(\mathcal{T}_0G:=\check{m_G}\in \mathcal S'(\mathbb {R})\), i.e. the tempered distribution with \(\widehat{\mathcal{T}_0G}=m_G\). \(\mathcal{T}_0\) is \(\mathbb {R}\)-linear and its definition does not involve \(\gamma \). For admissible \(\gamma \), \(\widetilde{Y}_\gamma :=\{ G\in Y_\gamma :\ell (G)=0\} \) (as in definition 2.10). We say \(\mathcal{T}_0G\in X_\gamma \) if there is \(r\in X_\gamma \) with \(\widehat r=m_G\); this \(r\) is unique and is identified with \(\mathcal{T}_0G\).

Definition 2.3Correction space \(X_\gamma \)

Let \(\gamma \in \mathbb {R}\). For \(r\in W^{2,\infty }_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb {R};\mathbb {R})\) (equivalently: \(r\in C^1(\mathbb {R})\) with \(r'\) locally Lipschitz; then \(r''\) exists a.e. and is in \(L^\infty _{\mathrm{loc}}\)) set

\[ \| r\| _{X_\gamma }:=\operatorname *{ess\, sup}_{y\ge 0}\langle y \rangle ^\gamma \bigl(|r(y)|+\langle y \rangle ^{-1/p}|r'(y)|+\langle y \rangle ^{-2/p}|r''(y)|\bigr) +\operatorname *{ess\, sup}_{y\le 0}\langle y \rangle ^\gamma \bigl(|r(y)|+\langle y \rangle |r'(y)|+\langle y \rangle ^{2}|r''(y)|\bigr)\in [0,\infty ], \]

and \(X_\gamma :=\{ r\in W^{2,\infty }_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb {R};\mathbb {R}):\| r\| _{X_\gamma }{\lt}\infty \} \), a real normed space.

Lemma 3.12The nonperturbative coefficient

Let \(1{\lt}\alpha {\lt}2\), \(0\le \epsilon \le 1\), \(W(y)=\max \{ -y,0\} \) and let \(\chi _+\in C^\infty (\mathbb {R})\) with \(\chi _+=1\) on \([2,\infty )\), \(\chi _+=0\) on \((-\infty ,1]\). For \(y{\gt}1\) the integral \(\int _\mathbb {R}\frac{\partial _1\Gamma _\epsilon (W'(y),S_W(y,z))}{|y-z|^\alpha }dz\) converges absolutely; define \(b_\epsilon (y)\) as \(\chi _+(y)\) times this integral for \(y{\gt}1\), and \(b_\epsilon (y)=0\) for \(y\le 1\). Then

\[ b_\epsilon (y)=c_\epsilon \chi _+(y)y^{-p}\ (y\in \mathbb {R}),\qquad c_\epsilon =c_\alpha \int _0^1\bigl[(1+\epsilon t^2)^{-\alpha /2}-1\bigr](1-t)^{p-1}dt, \]

and \(|c_\epsilon |\le \frac{c_\alpha \alpha }{2p}\epsilon \). (In particular \(c_0=0\).)

Lemma 3.81Stationary phase against a tail integral

Let \(x_0\in \mathbb {R}\), \(L{\gt}0\), \(I=(x_0-L,x_0+L)\), \(\kappa {\gt}0\), \(A,M\ge 0\), \(\omega ,\omega _0\in \mathbb {R}\), and constants \(c_1,\dots ,c_4{\gt}0\). Assume:

  1. \(\Phi \in C^3(\overline{I};\mathbb {R})\), \(\Phi '(x_0)=0\), \(c_1\kappa \le |\Phi ''|\le c_2\kappa \) and \(|\Phi '''|\le c_3\kappa L^{-1}\) on \(I\);

  2. \(a\in C^2_c(I;\mathbb {C})\) with \(|a^{(j)}|\le c_4AL^{-j}\), \(j=0,1,2\);

  3. \(\Psi \in C([x_0-L,\infty );\mathbb {R})\) is such that \(E(t)=\int _t^\infty e^{i\Psi (s)}ds\) exists (improper) for every \(t\in I\), and \(|E(t)|\le M\) on \(I\);

  4. \(\Phi (t)+\Psi (t)=\omega t+\omega _0\) for \(t\in I\).

Then \(\bigl|\int _Ia(t)e^{i\Phi (t)}E(t)dt\bigr|\le C\, A(M\kappa ^{-1/2}+\kappa ^{-1})\) with \(C=C(c_1,\dots ,c_4)\).

Lemma 1.9Distributional meaning

Let \(g\in L^\infty (\mathbb {R})\cap W^{1,\infty }_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb {R})\) with \(|g'(y)|\le C\langle y \rangle ^N\) a.e. for some \(C,N\ge 0\). Then \(|D|^pg\) (pointwise, definition 1.5) is continuous, satisfies \(\bigl||D|^pg(y)\bigr|\le C'\langle y \rangle ^N\), and for every \(\varphi \in \mathcal S(\mathbb {R})\)

\[ \int _\mathbb {R}|D|^pg(y)\, \varphi (y)\, dy=\int _\mathbb {R}g(y)\, |D|^p\varphi (y)\, dy , \]

where \(|D|^p\varphi =(|\xi |^p\widehat\varphi )^\vee \) satisfies \(|\, |D|^p\varphi (y)|\le C_\varphi \langle y \rangle ^{-\alpha }\). In particular the pointwise \(|D|^pg\) coincides with the distribution \(\varphi \mapsto \langle g,|D|^p\varphi \rangle \), so a pointwise identity \(\mathcal{E}_\epsilon (f)=0\) on \(\mathbb {R}\) (definition 1.26) for \(f\in \mathcal A\) with \(f''\) of polynomial growth implies \(\mathcal{E}_\epsilon (f)=0\) in \(\mathcal D'(\mathbb {R})\).

Lemma 2.16\(\Pi \) is a bounded projection onto \(\widetilde{Y}_\gamma \)

Let \(\gamma \) be admissible and let \(C_\ell (\gamma )\) be a constant with \(|\ell (G)|\le C_\ell (\gamma )\| G\| _{Y_\gamma }\) for \(G\in Y_\gamma \) (which exists by proposition 8.39). Then:

  1. \(\widetilde{Y}_\gamma \) is a closed \(\mathbb {R}\)-linear subspace of \(Y_\gamma \) (hence a Banach space);

  2. \(\Pi :Y_\gamma \to Y_\gamma \) is \(\mathbb {R}\)-linear with \(\| \Pi G\| _{Y_\gamma }\le \bigl(1+C_\ell (\gamma )(\| G_+\| _{Y_\gamma }+\| G_-\| _{Y_\gamma })\bigr)\| G\| _{Y_\gamma }\);

  3. \(\ell (\Pi G)=0\), i.e. \(\Pi (Y_\gamma )\subset \widetilde{Y}_\gamma \); \(\Pi G=G\) for \(G\in \widetilde{Y}_\gamma \); hence \(\Pi ^2=\Pi \);

  4. \(\Pi G_\mu =0\) for all \(\mu \in \mathbb {C}\), and \(\Pi G=G-G_\mu \) whenever \(\ell (G)=1-\mu /\mu _*\).

Lemma 3.5Bounds on \(A_\epsilon \)

Let \(1{\lt}\alpha {\lt}2\), \(0\le \epsilon \le 1\) and \(R\ge 1\). Then \(0{\lt}A_\epsilon \le 1\), \(A_\epsilon (0)=1\), \(A_\epsilon '(0)=0\), \(A_\epsilon '(s)=-\alpha \epsilon s(1+\epsilon s^2)^{-\alpha /2-1}\), so \(|A_\epsilon '(s)|\le \alpha \epsilon |s|\) and \(|1-A_\epsilon (s)|\le \frac\alpha 2\epsilon s^2\) for all \(s\in \mathbb {R}\). Lemma 3.72Conversion of Euler bounds to ordinary derivatives

Let \(F\in C^\infty ((0,\infty );\mathbb {C})\) and \(E=y\partial _y\). For \(j\in \mathbb {N}\) define real coefficients \(a_{j,l}\) by \(\prod _{r=0}^{j-1}(X-r)=\sum _{l=0}^j a_{j,l}X^l\). Then \(y^j F^{(j)}(y)=\sum _{l=0}^j a_{j,l}E^lF(y)\) for \(y{\gt}0\). Lemma 3.28Localization of the fractional operator

Fix \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\), \(s{\gt}0\), \(s\notin \mathbb {N}\), and \(\eta \in C_c^\infty (\mathbb {R};[0,1])\), \(\eta =1\) on \([-2,2]\), \(\operatorname {supp}\eta \subset [-3,3]\). Suppose \(g\) is bounded and locally Lipschitz, \(g\in C^s_{\rm loc}(\mathbb {R})\), and \(h=|D|^pg\in C^s_{\rm loc}(\mathbb {R})\), with the defining singular integral absolutely convergent. Then \(v=\eta g\) is compactly supported and globally Lipschitz, \(v\in C^s(\mathbb {R})\), and on \([-1,1]\)

\[ |D|^pv=h-T,\qquad T(y)=-c_p\int _\mathbb {R}(1-\eta (z))g(z)|z-y|^{-1-p}\, dz. \]

The displayed integral and all its \(y\) derivatives converge absolutely on \([-1,1]\); \(T\) is smooth on \((-2,2)\) and \(\sup _{|y|\le 1}|T^{(j)}(y)|\le C(p,j,\eta )\| g\| _\infty \). In particular \(|D|^pv\in C^s([-1,1])\).

Lemma 3.19Hölder product and composition estimates

Let \(s{\gt}0\), \(s\notin \mathbb {N}\), and \(I\) a compact interval of length \(|I|\ge 1\). There is \(C=C(s)\) such that for \(a,b\in C^s(I)\):

Lemma 3.53A finite sequence of integrations by parts

Let \(U\subset \mathbb {R}\) be open, \(n\in \mathbb {N}\), \(\phi \in C^{n+1}(U;\mathbb {R})\) with \(\phi '\ne 0\) on \(U\), and \(a\in C_c^n(U;\mathbb {C})\), extended by zero to \(\mathbb {R}\). Set \(L_\phi a=(a/(i\phi '))'\) on \(U\) and zero outside \(U\), and iterate this definition. For \(0\le j\le n\), \(L_\phi ^j a\) is continuous, compactly supported in \(\operatorname {supp}a\), and belongs to \(C^{n-j}(\mathbb {R})\). All the following integrals converge absolutely:

\[ \int _\mathbb {R}a(x)e^{i\phi (x)}\, dx=(-1)^n\int _\mathbb {R}L_\phi ^n a(x)e^{i\phi (x)}\, dx. \]

The values chosen for \(\phi \) outside \(U\) do not affect either side.

Lemma 3.85Integration by parts against the homogeneous kernel

Let \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\), \(\Lambda {\gt}0\), \(B\ge 0\), \(K{\gt}p\), and \(c_0,(C_s)_{s\ge 0}\) constants. Then for all \(\eta \ge 0\)

\[ \Bigl|\int _\mathbb {R}e^{i\phi (z)}e^{-\eta z^2}\frac{b(z)}{|z|^{1+p}}dz\Bigr|\le C B\Lambda ^{p-K}, \]

with \(C\) depending only on \(p,K,c_0\) and finitely many \(C_s\); and the integral is continuous in \(\eta \ge 0\).

Let \(s=k+\theta \notin \mathbb {N}\), \(I\) a compact interval, \((T,\nu )\) a \(\sigma \)-finite measure space and \(H:I\times T\to \mathbb {C}\) such that for \(\nu \)-a.e. \(\tau \), \(H(\cdot ,\tau )\in C^s(I)\), the maps \((x,\tau )\mapsto \partial _x^iH(x,\tau )\), \(i\le k\), are measurable, and \(\int _T\| H(\cdot ,\tau )\| _{C^s(I)}d\nu (\tau ){\lt}\infty \). Lemma 3.77Integrable parameter-derivative majorants for the far representation

With \(a_n\) as in lemma 3.75, for every \(n,j\in \mathbb {N}\) there is \(C=C(p,m,n,j,\chi _{\rm sp},C_0,\ldots ,C_{n+j+2})\) such that for \(y,\xi \ge 1\),

\[ |\partial _y^j(a_n(y,\xi )e^{i\phi _y(\xi )})| \le C\xi ^{m-n+j}(y+\xi ^p)^{-n} \le C y^{-n/2}\xi ^{m-n+j-pn/2}. \]

\[ \sup _{|y|\le Y}|F_M^\rho (a;y)-F(y)| \le C M^{m-N(1+p)+1}\qquad (M\ge 2L). \]

Lemma 4.8Iterated symbol bounds from a finite recurrence

Let \(L,m,\sigma ,A,H,b,q\) satisfy the regularity and support hypotheses of lemma 4.7, and let nonnegative sequences \((B_r),(D_r)\) satisfy its derivative bounds for every \(r\in \mathbb {N}\). Define nonnegative coefficients by the finite recurrence

\[ E_{0,k}=B_k,\qquad E_{n+1,k}=\sum _{r=0}^{k+1}\binom {k+1}{r}E_{n,r}D_{k+1-r}. \]

For all \(N,k\in \mathbb {N}\), \(T_q^Nb\) is smooth, vanishes on \((-\infty ,L]\), has support contained in \(\operatorname {supp}b\), and

\[ |\partial _\xi ^kT_q^Nb(\xi )| \le E_{N,k}AH^N\xi ^{m-N(1+\sigma )-k}\qquad (\xi \ge L). \]

The coefficient \(E_{N,k}\) depends only on \(N,k\) and \(B_0,\ldots ,B_{N+k},D_0,\ldots ,D_{N+k}\). If \(d:=m-N(1+\sigma ){\lt}-1\), then \(T_q^Nb\in L^1((0,\infty ))\) and

\[ \int _0^\infty |T_q^Nb(\xi )|d\xi \le E_{N,0}AH^N\frac{L^{d+1}}{-d-1}. \]

No compact-support hypothesis is imposed on \(b\) in this lemma.

Lemma 4.7One integration-by-parts step: flat extension and symbol bound

Let \(L\ge 1\), \(m,\sigma \in \mathbb {R}\), \(A,H{\gt}0\), \(b\in C^\infty (\mathbb {R};\mathbb {C})\) with \(b=0\) on \((-\infty ,L]\), and \(q\in C^\infty ((L/2,\infty );\mathbb {R})\). Set \(T_qb=-\partial _\xi (bq/i)\) on \((L,\infty )\) and \(T_qb=0\) on \((-\infty ,L]\). Then \(T_qb\in C^\infty (\mathbb {R};\mathbb {C})\), every derivative of \(T_qb\) vanishes on \((-\infty ,L]\), and \(\operatorname {supp}T_qb\subset \operatorname {supp}b\). For every \(k\in \mathbb {N}\) and \(\xi \ge L\),

\[ \partial _\xi ^kT_qb(\xi ) =i\sum _{r=0}^{k+1}\binom {k+1}{r}b^{(r)}(\xi )q^{(k+1-r)}(\xi ). \]

If nonnegative numbers \(B_0,\ldots ,B_{k+1}\) and \(D_0,\ldots ,D_{k+1}\) satisfy

\[ |b^{(r)}(\xi )|\le B_rA\xi ^{m-r},\qquad |q^{(r)}(\xi )|\le D_rH\xi ^{-\sigma -r} \quad (\xi \ge L,\ 0\le r\le k+1), \]

\[ |\partial _\xi ^kT_qb(\xi )|\le \left(\sum _{r=0}^{k+1}\binom {k+1}{r}B_rD_{k+1-r}\right) AH\xi ^{m-1-\sigma -k}\qquad (\xi \ge L). \]

Thus this one-step constant involves only the displayed finite lists and \(k\), and is independent of \(L,A,H,b,q\) once those bounds are fixed.

Lemma 4.9Repeated integration by parts with quantified symbol loss

Let \(L\ge 1\), \(m,\sigma \in \mathbb {R}\), and \(A,H{\gt}0\). Let \(b\in C^\infty (\mathbb {R};\mathbb {C})\) vanish on \((-\infty ,L]\), and let \(q\in C^\infty ((L/2,\infty );\mathbb {R})\) satisfy, for every \(r\in \mathbb {N}\) and \(\xi \ge L\),

\[ |b^{(r)}(\xi )|\le B_r A\xi ^{m-r},\qquad |q^{(r)}(\xi )|\le D_r H\xi ^{-\sigma -r}, \]

where \(B_r,D_r\ge 0\) are fixed. Define \(T_qb=-\partial _\xi (bq/i)\) on \((L,\infty )\), extended by zero to \((-\infty ,L]\), and iterate this operator. Every \(T_q^Nb\) is smooth and vanishes on \((-\infty ,L]\). For all \(N,k\in \mathbb {N}\) there is \(C_{N,k}{\gt}0\), depending only on \(N,k,m,\sigma \) and \(B_0,\ldots ,B_{N+k},D_0,\ldots ,D_{N+k}\), such that

\[ |\partial _\xi ^kT_q^Nb(\xi )| \le C_{N,k} A H^N\xi ^{m-N(1+\sigma )-k}\qquad (\xi \ge L). \]

Suppose in addition that \(b\) has compact support, \(\phi \in C^\infty ((0,\infty );\mathbb {R})\), and \(q(\xi )\phi '(\xi )=1\) for \(\xi {\gt}L\). Then all the following integrals converge absolutely and

\[ \int _0^\infty b(\xi )e^{i\phi (\xi )}d\xi =\int _0^\infty T_q^Nb(\xi )e^{i\phi (\xi )}d\xi \qquad (N\in \mathbb {N}). \]

Compact support of \(b\) is not needed for the symbol bound; if \(m-N(1+\sigma ){\lt}-1\), that bound makes \(T_q^Nb\) integrable on \((0,\infty )\).

Lemma 4.14Properties of \(\operatorname {Osc}\)

Let \(a\in S^m_+\).

  1. The limit defining \(\operatorname {Osc}[a](y)\) exists, locally uniformly in \(y\in \mathbb {R}\), and does not depend on \(\rho \). If \(a\in L^1\) it equals the Lebesgue integral \(\int _0^\infty ae^{i(y\xi -\Phi _0)}d\xi \); if \(m{\lt}p\) it equals the improper Riemann integral \(\lim _{M\to \infty }\int _0^M ae^{i(y\xi -\Phi _0)}d\xi \).

  2. \(\operatorname {Osc}[a]\in C^\infty (\mathbb {R})\) and \(\partial _y\operatorname {Osc}[a]=\operatorname {Osc}[i\xi a]\) (note \(i\xi a\in S^{m+1}_+\)).

  3. For all \(N\ge 0\) there is \(C\) (depending on \(N,m,p\) and finitely many \(C_l\)) with \(|\operatorname {Osc}[a](y)|\le C|y|^{-N}\) for \(y\le -1\).

Lemma 4.22Corner comparison as two absolutely convergent integrals

Let \(\frac34{\lt}p{\lt}1\) and, on \((0,\infty )\), put

\[ b(\xi )=(1-\chi _+(\xi ))\frac{1-e^{-i\Phi _0(\xi )}}{\xi ^2},\qquad a_{-2}(\xi )=\frac{\chi _+(\xi )}{\xi ^2}. \]

Both \(b\) and \(a_{-2}\) are integrable on \((0,\infty )\), and \(|b(\xi )|\le \xi ^{p-1}\mathbf1_{(0,2]}(\xi )\). Define the absolutely convergent integrals

\[ \mathcal{I}_1(y)=\frac1\pi \operatorname {Re}\int _0^\infty e^{iy\xi }b(\xi )d\xi , \qquad \mathcal{I}_2(y)=\frac1\pi \operatorname {Re}\int _0^\infty e^{iy\xi }a_{-2}(\xi )d\xi . \]

Then \(f_{0,\textup{low}}(y)-W(y)=\mathcal{I}_1(y)+\mathcal{I}_2(y)\) for every \(y\in \mathbb {R}\).

Lemma 6.6Elementary tail integrals

Lemma 6.4Differentiating translated fractional integrals

Let \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\) and \(w\in C^3(\mathbb {R})\) with \(\sup |w^{(k)}|\leq B_k{\lt}\infty \), \(k=1,2,3\) (\(B_k{\gt}0\)). \[ I(y)=\int _\mathbb {R}\frac{w'(y)-w'(y-s)}{|s|^{1+p}}\Phi (y,s)\, ds . \]

Then the integral converges absolutely for every \(y\), \(I\) is differentiable on \(\mathbb {R}\),

\[ I'(y)=\int _\mathbb {R}\frac{(w''(y)-w''(y-s))\Phi (y,s)+(w'(y)-w'(y-s))\partial _y\Phi (y,s)}{|s|^{1+p}}\, ds, \]

and, with \(C_p\) as in lemma 6.3,

\[ \partial _yS_f=\frac{f'(y)-S_f}{y-z},\qquad \partial _zS_f=\frac{S_f-f'(z)}{y-z},\qquad \partial _y\partial _zS_f=\frac{f'(y)+f'(z)-2S_f}{(y-z)^2}. \]

Lemma 8.27Fractional integration by parts against Schwartz functions

Let \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\), let \(w\in L^1(\mathbb {R};\mathbb {C})\) be bounded and locally Lipschitz, and suppose \(|w'(x)|\le A\langle x \rangle ^N\) a.e. for some \(A,N\ge 0\). For every \(\varphi \in \mathcal S(\mathbb {R};\mathbb {C})\),

Lemma 8.26Shifted fractional kernel: domination and continuity

Let \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\), \(A,M,N\ge 0\), and let \(w:\mathbb {R}\to \mathbb {C}\) be locally Lipschitz with \(|w(x)|\le M\) for every \(x\) and \(|w'(x)|\le A\langle x \rangle ^N\) for a.e. \(x\). For every \(B\ge 1\), \(|x|\le B\) and \(h\ne 0\),

\[ \frac{|w(x)-w(x-h)|}{|h|^{1+p}}\le A\langle B+1 \rangle ^N|h|^{-p}\mathbf1_{\{ 0{\lt}|h|\le 1\} } +2M|h|^{-1-p}\mathbf1_{\{ |h|{\gt}1\} }. \]

The right side is integrable in \(h\). Consequently the integral defining \(|D|^pw(x)\) is absolutely convergent for every \(x\), \(|D|^pw\) is continuous, and there is \(C_{p,N}{\gt}0\), independent of \(A,M,w,x\), such that \(|\, |D|^pw(x)|\le C_{p,N}(A+M)\langle x \rangle ^N\) for every \(x\).

Lemma 8.28The fractional multiplier in Schwartz-test form

Lemma 9.17Cutoff and amplitude bounds

There are constants \(c_*\in (0,1)\) and \(C_\ell \) (\(\ell \ge 0\)), depending only on \(p,\chi \), such that for all \(R\ge 2\), \(y\in \mathbb {R}\), \(\xi {\gt}0\), \(j\in \{ 0,1,2\} \):

  1. \(\chi _{\textup{s}}(y,\xi )\neq 0\Rightarrow y{\gt}0\) and \(|\xi -y^{1/p}|\le y^{1/p}/50\); \(\chi _{\textup{s}}(y,\xi )=1\) if \(y{\gt}0\) and \(|\xi -y^{1/p}|\le y^{1/p}/100\).

  2. \(|\partial _\xi ^\ell \chi _{\textup{s}}(y,\xi )|+|\partial _\xi ^\ell \chi _{\textup{ns}}(y,\xi )|\le C_\ell \xi ^{-\ell }\) for \(\ell \ge 1\), and \(0\le \chi _{\textup{s}},\chi _{\textup{ns}}\le 1\); moreover \(\int _0^\infty |\partial _\xi \chi _{\textup{ns}}(y,\xi )|d\xi \le C_0\).

  3. \(a_j^R\) is smooth on \((0,\infty )\), vanishes on \((0,1]\) with all derivatives, is supported in \([1,2R]\), and \(|\partial _\xi ^\ell a_j^R(\xi )|\le C_\ell \xi ^{j-2-\ell }\) (uniformly in \(R\)); \(\int _0^\infty |\partial _\xi [(1-\chi )\theta _R](\xi )|d\xi \le C_0\).

  4. If \(\chi _{\textup{ns}}(y,\xi )\neq 0\) (or \(\xi \) is in its support) and \(\xi \ge 1\) then \(|y-\xi ^p|\ge c_*(|y|+\xi ^p)\); and \(|y|+\xi ^p\ge 2^{-1/2}\langle y \rangle \) for \(\xi \ge 1\).

  5. If \(a_j^{\textup{s},R}(y,\xi )\neq 0\) then \(y\ge y_*:=(50/51)^p\), \(\frac{49}{50}y^{1/p}\le \xi \le \frac{51}{50}y^{1/p}\), and \(\langle y \rangle \le C_0\, y\).

Let \(\gamma \) be admissible.

  1. If \(r\in X_\gamma \) then \(|r^{(j)}(y)|\le \| r\| _{X_\gamma }w_{\gamma ,j}(y)\) for \(j=0,1\) and all \(y\), and for \(j=2\) and a.e. \(y\). Conversely, if \(r:\mathbb {R}\to \mathbb {R}\) is \(C^1\) with \(r'\) locally Lipschitz and \(|r^{(j)}|\le A\, w_{\gamma ,j}\) (\(j=0,1\) everywhere, \(j=2\) a.e.), then \(r\in X_\gamma \) and \(\| r\| _{X_\gamma }\le 6A\).

  2. If \(G\in Y_\gamma \) then \(|G(y)|\le \| G\| _{Y_\gamma }w_{\gamma ,0}(y)\) for all \(y\) and \(|G'(y)|\le \| G\| _{Y_\gamma }w_{\gamma ,1}(y)\) for a.e. \(y\); in particular \(|G'(y)|\le \| G\| _{Y_\gamma }\langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma +1/p}\le \| G\| _{Y_\gamma }\) a.e.

  3. There is \(C\) with \(\| G\| _{L^1}+\| G'\| _{L^1}+\int _\mathbb {R}|G'(z)|\, w_E(z)\, dz\le C\| G\| _{Y_\gamma }\) for all \(G\in Y_\gamma \).

  4. (Peetre) \(\langle a+b \rangle \le \sqrt2\, \langle a \rangle \langle b \rangle \) for \(a,b\in \mathbb {R}\); hence \(\langle y-z \rangle ^{-s}\le 2^{s/2}\langle y \rangle ^{-s}\langle z \rangle ^{s}\) for \(s\ge 0\).

  5. (Shifted derivative, paper eq. eqn:linear_nonstationary_shifted_derivative) There is \(C\) such that for \(G\in Y_\gamma \), every \(y\in \mathbb {R}\) and a.e. \(z\in \mathbb {R}\): \(|G'(y-z)|\le C\| G\| _{Y_\gamma }\langle z \rangle ^{\gamma +1}w_{\gamma ,1}(y)\).

  6. For every \(y,z\): \(|G(y-z)|\le 2^{\gamma /2}\| G\| _{Y_\gamma }\langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma }\langle z \rangle ^{\gamma }\).

Lemma 10.9Elementary bounds for \(B_\epsilon \)

Let \(0\le \epsilon \le 1\), \(R{\gt}0\), and \(B_\epsilon (u)=(1+\epsilon u^2)^{\alpha /2}\) with \(\alpha =p+1\in (1,2)\). Then for all \(|u|\le R\):

\[ |B_\epsilon (u)-1|\le \tfrac {\alpha }{2}\epsilon u^2,\qquad |B_\epsilon '(u)|\le \alpha \epsilon |u|,\qquad |B_\epsilon ''(u)|\le \alpha (1+R^2)\epsilon . \]

Lemma 10.19Quantitative removal of the diagonal cutoff

With exactly the kernel and cutoff hypotheses of lemma 10.18, let \(F(y)=\int H(y,z)dz\) and \(G(y)=\int J(y,z)dz\). The first integral converges absolutely for every \(y\in U\) and the second for a.e. \(y\in U\). For every \(0{\lt}\eta {\lt}1/2\),

\[ \sup _{y\in U}|F_\eta (y)-F(y)| \le \frac{2^{4-\alpha }}{3-\alpha }A\eta ^{3-\alpha }, \]
\[ \| G_\eta -G\| _{L^\infty (U)} \le A\left(\frac{2^{3-\alpha }}{2-\alpha } +\frac{2^{4-\alpha }M_\vartheta }{3-\alpha }\right)\eta ^{2-\alpha }. \]

The constants are independent of \(U,A,H,J,\eta \) apart from the displayed factors.

Lemma 10.18Weak derivative of a fixed-\(z\) truncation

Let \((H,J)\) be a dominated kernel pair on \(U\) with constant \(A\) and exponent \(1{\lt}\alpha {\lt}2\). Fix \(\vartheta \in C^\infty (\mathbb {R};[0,1])\) with \(\vartheta =0\) on \([-1,1]\) and \(\vartheta =1\) on \(\mathbb {R}\setminus (-2,2)\), and put \(M_\vartheta =\| \vartheta '\| _\infty \). For \(0{\lt}\eta {\lt}1/2\) define

\[ F_\eta (y)=\int _\mathbb {R}\vartheta ((y-z)/\eta )H(y,z)\, dz, \quad G_\eta (y)=\int _\mathbb {R}\left[\vartheta ((y-z)/\eta )J(y,z) +\eta ^{-1}\vartheta '((y-z)/\eta )H(y,z)\right]dz. \]

The value integral is absolutely convergent for every \(y\in U\), and both summands defining \(G_\eta \) are absolutely integrable for a.e. \(y\in U\). The actual function \(F_\eta \) is locally Lipschitz on \(U\), \(F_\eta '=G_\eta \) a.e. there, and

\[ \| G_\eta \| _{L^\infty (U)}\le A\left(\frac2{2-\alpha }+\frac2{\alpha -1} +\frac{2^{4-\alpha }M_\vartheta }{3-\alpha }\eta ^{2-\alpha }\right). \]

In particular, for every \(a{\lt}b\) with \([a,b]\subset U\), \(F_\eta (b)-F_\eta (a)=\int _a^bG_\eta (y)\, dy\).

Then \(\Delta B_\epsilon \in W^{1,\infty }_{\mathrm{loc}}\) and there is \(C=C(p,\gamma ,M,N)\) such that for a.e. \(y\) (paper eq:N1_delta_B_bound, eq:N1_delta_B_derivative_bound)

\[ |\Delta B_\epsilon (y)|\le C\epsilon \| r_1-r_2\| _{X_\gamma }\begin{cases} \langle y \rangle ^{-\beta -\gamma +1/p},& y\ge 0\\ \langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma -1},& y\le 0\end{cases}, \quad |\partial _y\Delta B_\epsilon (y)|\le C\epsilon \| r_1-r_2\| _{X_\gamma }\begin{cases} \langle y \rangle ^{-\beta -\gamma +2/p},& y\ge 0\\ \langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma -2},& y\le 0.\end{cases} \]

Lemma 10.26Elementary integrals

Let \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\), \(\alpha =1+p\). There is \(C=C(p)\) such that for all \(\lambda \ge 1\) and \(a{\gt}0\):

\[ \int _\mathbb {R}\frac{\min \{ 1,\lambda |\rho |\} ^2}{|\rho |^{1+p}}d\rho =C_2\lambda ^p,\quad \int _\mathbb {R}\frac{\min \{ 1,\lambda |\rho |\} }{|\rho |^{1+p}}d\rho =C_1\lambda ^p,\quad \int _{|\rho |\le a}|\rho |^{1-p}d\rho =\tfrac {2a^{2-p}}{2-p},\quad \int _{|\rho |\le a}|\rho |^{-p}d\rho =\tfrac {2a^{1-p}}{1-p}, \]
\[ \int _{|\rho |\ge a}|\rho |^{-\alpha }d\rho =\tfrac {2}{p}a^{-p},\qquad \int _{|\rho |\ge a}|\rho |^{-\alpha -1}d\rho =\tfrac {2}{1+p}a^{-1-p},\qquad \int _{|\rho |\ge a}|\rho |^{-\alpha -2}d\rho =\tfrac {2}{2+p}a^{-2-p}, \]

with \(C_1,C_2\le C\). Moreover, for \(\gamma {\gt}1\) and \(|y|\ge 2\), with \(C_\gamma =\int \langle z \rangle ^{-\gamma }dz\),

\[ \int _{|y-z|\ge |y|/2}\frac{\langle z \rangle ^{-\gamma }}{|y-z|^{\alpha +k}}dz\le 2^{\alpha +k}C_\gamma |y|^{-\alpha -k} \le 2^{2\alpha +2k}C_\gamma \langle y \rangle ^{-\alpha -k},\qquad k=1,2. \]

In applications \(\lambda =\langle y \rangle ^{1/p}\), so \(\lambda ^p=\langle y \rangle \); and \(a=|y|/2\) with \(|y|\ge 2\), so \(a\ge \langle y \rangle /4\).

Lemma 10.31Far-field integrand bounds, \(y\ge 2\)

With the standing assumptions, \(y\ge 2\), \(|y-z|\ge y/2\), and \(\widetilde K\) as in lemma 10.30:

Lemma 10.30Model coefficient subtraction

For \(y\ge 2\) and every \(z{\lt}0\), \(S_W(y,z)=\frac{z}{y-z}\in (-1,0)\) and \(\partial _yS_W(y,z)=-\frac{S_W(y,z)}{y-z}\); for \(z\ge 0\), \(z\ne y\), \(S_W(y,z)=0\). Consequently, for \(y\ge 2\) (paper eq:N3_model_coefficient)

\[ b_\epsilon (y)=\int _{z{\lt}0}\frac{\partial _1\Gamma _\epsilon (0,S_W(y,z))}{|y-z|^\alpha }dz =\int _{|y-z|\ge y/2}\frac{\partial _1\Gamma _\epsilon (0,S_W(y,z))}{|y-z|^\alpha }dz, \]

hence, writing \(\widetilde K(y,z)=K_{f,h}(y,z)-\partial _1\Gamma _\epsilon (0,S_W(y,z))h'(y)\), (paper eq:N3_far_subtraction, eq:N3_far_subtraction_derivative)

\[ \int _{|y-z|\ge y/2}\frac{K_{f,h}}{|y-z|^\alpha }dz-b_\epsilon (y)h'(y)=\int _{|y-z|\ge y/2}\frac{\widetilde K(y,z)}{|y-z|^\alpha }dz, \]

and for a.e. \(y{\gt}2\)

\[ \int _{|y-z|\ge y/2}\frac{\partial _yK_{f,h}-\alpha K_{f,h}/(y-z)}{|y-z|^\alpha }dz-\partial _y(b_\epsilon h')(y) =\int _{|y-z|\ge y/2}\frac{1}{|y-z|^\alpha }\Bigl(\partial _y-\frac{\alpha }{y-z}\Bigr)\widetilde K(y,z)\, dz . \]

(Here \(\partial _y\) acts with \(z\) fixed; the integration region is not differentiated.)

Lemma 10.38Difference estimate away from the diagonal on a compact set

Let \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\), \(\alpha =1+p\), \(R\ge 1\), \(S\ge 5R\), \(0{\lt}\delta {\lt}1\), and \(B,L\ge 1\). There exists \(C=C(p,R,S,\delta ,B,L){\gt}0\) such that for every \(0\le \epsilon \le 1\) and \(g_0,g_1\in W^{2,\infty }_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb {R})\) satisfying \(\| g_j'\| _{L^\infty (\mathbb {R})}\le B\) and \(\| g_j''\| _{L^\infty ([-S,S])}\le L\) (\(j=0,1\)), the following holds. Put

\[ e_S=\| g_1-g_0\| _{L^\infty ([-S,S])} +\| g_1'-g_0'\| _{L^\infty ([-S,S])} +\| g_1''-g_0''\| _{L^\infty ([-S,S])},\qquad E_y=\{ z:|z|\le S,\ |y-z|\ge \delta \} . \]

The value-difference integrand below is absolutely integrable on \(E_y\) for every \(|y|\le R\), and the derivative-difference integrand is absolutely integrable there for a.e. \(|y|\le R\). Using \(K_g^{(1)}\) from lemma 10.37,

\[ \sup _{|y|\le R}\int _{E_y} \frac{|\Gamma _\epsilon (g_1'(y),S_{g_1})-\Gamma _\epsilon (g_0'(y),S_{g_0})|}{|y-z|^\alpha }dz \le C\epsilon e_S, \]
\[ \mathop{\mathrm{ess\, sup}}_{|y|\le R}\int _{E_y} \frac{|K_{g_1}^{(1)}(y,z)-K_{g_0}^{(1)}(y,z)|}{|y-z|^\alpha }dz \le C\epsilon e_S. \]

The inequalities remain valid if \(E_y\) is replaced by any measurable subset.

Lemma 10.37Local \(W^{1,\infty }\) structure of \(\mathcal{I}_\epsilon \)

Let \(0\le \epsilon \le 1\), \(g\in W^{2,\infty }_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb {R})\) with \(g'\in L^\infty (\mathbb {R})\), and set, for \(z\ne y\),

with \(S_g=S_g(y,z)\). \[ |K_{f,h}|\le C\epsilon \| h\| \begin{cases} \langle y \rangle ^{-2\beta -\gamma +1/p}m^2,& y\ge 2\\ \langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma -p-4}|y-z|^2,& y\le -2\end{cases}, \]
\[ |\partial _yK_{f,h}|+\frac{|K_{f,h}|}{|y-z|}\le C\epsilon \| h\| \begin{cases} \langle y \rangle ^{-2\beta -\gamma +2/p}m,& y\ge 2\\ \langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma -p-4}|y-z|,& y\le -2,\end{cases} \]

with \(m=m(y,z)\) as in lemma 10.27.

Lemma 10.24Variation formula for \(\mathcal{N}_3\)

Let \(0\le \epsilon \le 1\), \(\beta +\frac1p{\lt}\gamma {\lt}2p+1\), \(\overline{f}\) admissible with constant \(M\), and \(r,h\in X_\gamma \). Then:

  1. for every \(y\) the integral defining \(D\mathcal{N}_3(r)[h](y)\) converges absolutely;

  2. for every \(y\), the map \(t\mapsto \mathcal{N}_3(r+th)(y)\) is \(C^1\) on \(\mathbb {R}\) with derivative \(D\mathcal{N}_3(r+th)[h](y)\);

  3. \(D\mathcal{N}_3(r)[h]\in W^{1,\infty }_{\mathrm{loc}}\) and its weak derivative is (paper eq:N3_variation_derivative)

    \[ \partial _yD\mathcal{N}_3(r)[h](y)=\int _\mathbb {R}\frac{\partial _yK_{f,h}(y,z)-\alpha K_{f,h}(y,z)/(y-z)}{|y-z|^\alpha }\, dz-\partial _y(b_\epsilon h')(y), \]

    where \(\partial _yK_{f,h}\) is computed by the chain rule using lemma 10.15, and the integral converges absolutely for a.e. \(y\).

Lemma 10.43Uniform estimates for admissible profiles

Let \(\beta +\frac1p{\lt}\gamma {\lt}2p+1\), \(M,N{\gt}0\), \(0\le \epsilon \le \min \{ 1,\epsilon _0\} \) (\(\epsilon _0\) of lemma 8.25), and \(\overline{f}\) an admissible profile with constant \(M\) to which lemma 10.2 applies. There is \(C=C(p,\gamma ,M,N)\), independent of \(\epsilon \) and \(\overline{f}\), such that for all \(r,r_1,r_2\in X_\gamma \) with norms \(\le N\), \(\mathcal{N}_{\epsilon ,\overline{f}}(r)\in Y_\gamma \) and

\[ \| \mathcal{N}_{\epsilon ,\overline{f}}(r_1)-\mathcal{N}_{\epsilon ,\overline{f}}(r_2)\| _{Y_\gamma }\le C\epsilon \| r_1-r_2\| _{X_\gamma },\qquad \| \mathcal{N}_{\epsilon ,\overline{f}}(r)\| _{Y_\gamma }\le C\epsilon \| r\| _{X_\gamma }. \]
LaTeX Lean
Lemma 10.2Decomposition of \(\mathcal{N}_{\epsilon ,\overline{f}}\)

Let \(\beta +\frac1p{\lt}\gamma {\lt}2p+1\), let \(0\le \epsilon \le \min \{ 1,\epsilon _0\} \) where \(\epsilon _0\) is the constant of lemma 8.25 (so that \(\mathcal{R}_\epsilon \) of definition 8.9 is defined), let \(\overline{f}\in C^2(\mathbb {R})\) with \(\overline{f}'\in L^\infty (\mathbb {R})\) and \(\overline{f}''\in L^\infty _{\mathrm{loc}}\), and such that \(|D|^p\overline{f}'\) is defined in the sense of definition 1.5; let \(r\in X_\gamma \). Then \(\mathcal{E}_\epsilon (\overline{f}+r)\) and \(\mathcal{E}_\epsilon (\overline{f})\) are defined, and for every \(y\in \mathbb {R}\)

\[ \mathcal{N}_{\epsilon ,\overline{f}}(r) =\mathcal{E}_\epsilon (\overline{f}+r)-\mathcal{E}_\epsilon (\overline{f})-\mathcal{L}_\epsilon r =\mathcal{N}_1(r)+\mathcal{N}_2(r)+\mathcal{N}_3(r)-\mathcal{R}_\epsilon r . \]

In particular \(\mathcal{N}_{\epsilon ,\overline{f}}(0)=0\).

Lemma 10.41Local convergence of the nonlinear operator

Let \(0\le \epsilon \le 1\), \(\beta +\frac1p{\lt}\gamma {\lt}2p+1\), \(r\in X_\gamma \), and let \(\overline{f}_k\) be admissible with a common constant \(M\) with \(\overline{f}_k\to \overline{f}\) in \(C^2_{\mathrm{loc}}\). Then for \(j=1,2,3\) and every \(R{\gt}0\), \(\mathcal{N}_j^{\epsilon ,\overline{f}_k}(r)\to \mathcal{N}_j^{\epsilon ,\overline{f}}(r)\) in \(W^{1,\infty }([-R,R])\).

Lemma 10.27Near-field increments

With the standing assumptions, let \(|y|\ge 2\) and \(|y-z|\le |y|/2\) (so \(z\) has the sign of \(y\) and \(\frac12\langle y \rangle \le \langle w \rangle \le 2\langle y \rangle \) for \(w\in I_{y,z}\)). Then, with \(m(y,z)=\min \{ 1,\langle y \rangle ^{1/p}|y-z|\} \), for \(y\ge 2\) (paper eq:N3_profile_increment, eq:N3_direction_increment):

\[ |f'(y)|+|S_f(y,z)|\le C\langle y \rangle ^{-\beta },\qquad |f'(y)-S_f(y,z)|\le C\langle y \rangle ^{-\beta }m(y,z),\qquad |f''(y)|+|\partial _yS_f(y,z)|\le C\langle y \rangle ^{-\beta +1/p}, \]
\[ |h'(y)|\le \| h\| \langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma +1/p},\quad |h'(y)-S_h(y,z)|\le C\| h\| \langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma +1/p}m(y,z),\quad |h''(y)|+|\partial _yS_h(y,z)|\le C\| h\| \langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma +2/p}, \]

and for \(y\le -2\):

\[ |f'(y)|+|S_f(y,z)|\le C,\quad |f'(y)-S_f(y,z)|\le C\langle y \rangle ^{-p-2}|y-z|,\quad |f''(y)|+|\partial _yS_f(y,z)|\le C\langle y \rangle ^{-p-2}, \]
\[ |h'(y)|\le \| h\| \langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma -1},\quad |h'(y)-S_h(y,z)|\le C\| h\| \langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma -2}|y-z|,\quad |h''(y)|+|\partial _yS_h(y,z)|\le C\| h\| \langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma -2}. \]

(Second-derivative statements hold for a.e. \(y\).)

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 10.23Differentiation in the profile parameter

Let \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\), \(\alpha =1+p\), \(0\le \epsilon \le 1\), and let \(f,h\in W^{2,\infty }_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb {R})\) have bounded first derivatives. For every \(y\in \mathbb {R}\), the function \(t\mapsto \mathcal{I}_\epsilon (f+th)(y)\) is \(C^1\) on \(\mathbb {R}\), all its defining integrals are absolutely convergent, and

\[ \frac{d}{dt}\mathcal{I}_\epsilon (f+th)(y) =\int _\mathbb {R}K_{f+th,h}(y,z)|y-z|^{-\alpha }\, dz. \]

The derivative integral is absolutely convergent for every \((t,y)\). Quantitatively, for every \(B,L\ge 1\) and \(T\ge 0\) there is \(C=C(p,B,L,T){\gt}0\) such that if \(R\ge 1\), \(\| f'\| _\infty ,\| h'\| _\infty \le B\) and \(\| f''\| _{L^\infty ([-R-2,R+2])},\| h''\| _{L^\infty ([-R-2,R+2])}\le L\), then for all \(|y|{\lt}R\), \(|t|\le T\), and \(z\ne y\),

\[ |\Gamma _\epsilon ((f+th)'(y),S_{f+th}(y,z))| +|K_{f+th,h}(y,z)|\le C\epsilon \min \{ |y-z|^2,1\} . \]

Thus one integrable majorant in \(z\) works for all \(t\in [-T,T]\) at each fixed \(y\).

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 10.7Consequences of admissibility and of \(X_\gamma \) membership

Let \(\beta +\frac1p{\lt}\gamma {\lt}2p+1\), \(M,N{\gt}0\), \(\overline{f}\) admissible with constant \(M\), \(r\in X_\gamma \) with \(\| r\| _{X_\gamma }\le N\), and \(f=\overline{f}+r\). There is \(C=C(p,\gamma ,M,N)\) such that:

  1. \(\| f'\| _{L^\infty (\mathbb {R})}\le C\), \(\| f\| _{L^\infty ([-3,3])}+\| f''\| _{L^\infty ([-3,3])}\le C\), and \(|f(y)-W(y)|\le C\langle y \rangle ^{-p}\) for all \(y\); the same holds with \(f\) replaced by \(\overline{f}\).

  2. For \(y\ge 0\): \(|f'(y)|\le C\langle y \rangle ^{-\beta }\) and \(|f''(y)|\le C\langle y \rangle ^{-\beta +1/p}\).

  3. For \(y\le 0\): \(|f'(y)+1|\le C\langle y \rangle ^{-p-1}\) and \(|f''(y)|\le C\langle y \rangle ^{-p-2}\).

  4. For every \(h\in X_\gamma \): \(\| h\| _{L^\infty }\le \| h\| _{X_\gamma }\), \(\| h\| _{L^1}\le C_\gamma \| h\| _{X_\gamma }\) with \(C_\gamma =\int _\mathbb {R}\langle z \rangle ^{-\gamma }dz{\lt}\infty \), and

    \[ |h'(y)|\le \| h\| _{X_\gamma }\begin{cases} \langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma +1/p},& y\ge 0\\ \langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma -1},& y\le 0\end{cases}, \qquad |h''(y)|\le \| h\| _{X_\gamma }\begin{cases} \langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma +2/p},& y\ge 0\\ \langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma -2},& y\le 0.\end{cases} \]

    In particular \(\| h'\| _{L^\infty }\le \| h\| _{X_\gamma }\) and \(\| h''\| _{L^\infty ([-3,3])}\le 10^{2/p}\| h\| _{X_\gamma }\).

Lemma 10.22Local domination for the profile kernel

Let \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\), \(\alpha =1+p\), and \(B,L\ge 1\). There exists \(C=C(p,B,L){\gt}0\) such that for every \(R\ge 1\), \(0\le \epsilon \le 1\), and \(g\in W^{2,\infty }_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb {R})\) with \(\| g'\| _{L^\infty (\mathbb {R})}\le B\) and \(\| g''\| _{L^\infty ([-R-2,R+2])}\le L\), the pair

\[ H_g(y,z)=\frac{\Gamma _\epsilon (g'(y),S_g(y,z))}{|y-z|^\alpha }, \]
\[ J_g(y,z)=\frac{1}{|y-z|^\alpha }\left[ \partial _1\Gamma _\epsilon (g'(y),S_g)g''(y) +\partial _2\Gamma _\epsilon (g'(y),S_g)\frac{g'(y)-S_g}{y-z} -\alpha \frac{\Gamma _\epsilon (g'(y),S_g)}{y-z}\right], \]

with diagonal values zero and \(g^{\prime \prime }\) taken to be the classical derivative where it exists and zero otherwise, is a dominated kernel pair on \((-R,R)\) with constant \(C\epsilon \). For the value numerator the bound is pointwise; for the derivative numerator it holds outside a null set of \(y\) independent of \(z\). These envelope inequalities hold also for \(|y|\le R\), pointwise for \(H_g\) and a.e. for \(J_g\). The same conclusion on \((-R,R)\) holds with the local second-derivative hypothesis only on \([-2R,2R]\), provided \(R\ge 1\), by using \(|y-z|\le 1\) in the near region.

Lemma 10.15Secant identities

Let \(g\in W^{2,\infty }_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb {R})\) and \(y\ne z\). Then \(S_g(y,z)=\int _0^1g'(z+t(y-z))\, dt\); \(y\mapsto S_g(y,z)\) is \(C^1\) on \(\mathbb {R}\setminus \{ z\} \) with (paper eq:N3_secant_derivatives)

\[ \partial _yS_g(y,z)=\frac{g'(y)-S_g(y,z)}{y-z}; \]

and, writing \(I_{y,z}\) for the closed segment between \(y\) and \(z\),

\[ |g'(y)-S_g(y,z)|\le |y-z|\, \| g''\| _{L^\infty (I_{y,z})},\quad |\partial _yS_g(y,z)|\le \| g''\| _{L^\infty (I_{y,z})},\quad |\partial _yS_g(y,z)|\le \frac{2\| g'\| _{L^\infty }}{|y-z|}, \]
\[ |S_g(y,z)|\le \min \Bigl\{ \| g'\| _{L^\infty },\ \frac{|g(y)|+|g(z)|}{|y-z|}\Bigr\} . \]

Lemma 10.8Transport-factor bounds

Let \(\beta +\frac1p{\lt}\gamma {\lt}2p+1\) and \(\overline{f}\) admissible with constant \(M\). There is \(C=C(p,M)\) such that (paper eq:N1_profile_factor, eq:N1_profile_factor_derivative)

\[ |\overline{f}-y\overline{f}'|\le C\begin{cases} \langle y \rangle ^{1-\beta },& y\ge 0\\ \langle y \rangle ^{-p},& y\le 0\end{cases},\qquad |\partial _y(\overline{f}-y\overline{f}')|=|y\overline{f}''|\le C\begin{cases} \langle y \rangle ^{1-\beta +1/p},& y\ge 0\\ \langle y \rangle ^{-p-1},& y\le 0,\end{cases} \]

and for every \(r\in X_\gamma \) and a.e. \(y\) (paper eq:N2_transport_bound, eq:N2_transport_derivative_bound)

\[ |r-yr'|\le 2\| r\| _{X_\gamma }\begin{cases} \langle y \rangle ^{1-\gamma +1/p},& y\ge 0\\ \langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma },& y\le 0\end{cases},\qquad |\partial _y(r-yr')|=|yr''|\le \| r\| _{X_\gamma }\begin{cases} \langle y \rangle ^{1-\gamma +2/p},& y\ge 0\\ \langle y \rangle ^{-\gamma -1},& y\le 0.\end{cases} \]

Lemma 10.21Local domination for the linearized kernel

Let \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\), \(\alpha =1+p\), and \(B,L\ge 1\). There exists \(C=C(p,B,L){\gt}0\) such that for every \(R\ge 1\), \(0\le \epsilon \le 1\), \(H_0\ge 0\), and \(f,h\in W^{2,\infty }_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb {R})\) satisfying

\[ \| f'\| _{L^\infty (\mathbb {R})}\le B,\quad \| h'\| _{L^\infty (\mathbb {R})}\le H_0,\quad \| f''\| _{L^\infty ([-R-2,R+2])}\le L,\quad \| h''\| _{L^\infty ([-R-2,R+2])}\le H_0, \]

the functions, set to zero on \(y=z\),

\[ H(y,z)=\frac{K_{f,h}(y,z)}{|y-z|^\alpha },\qquad J(y,z)=\frac{\partial _yK_{f,h}(y,z)-\alpha K_{f,h}(y,z)/(y-z)}{|y-z|^\alpha }, \]

form a dominated kernel pair on \(U=(-R,R)\) with constant \(C\epsilon H_0\). Here \(J\) is defined by the Borel chain-rule expression using the classical \(f^{\prime \prime }\) and \(h^{\prime \prime }\) where they exist and zero otherwise; its values on the common exceptional null set of \(y\) may be set to zero for every \(z\). More explicitly, for every \(y\in U,z\ne y\), \(|K_{f,h}(y,z)|\le C\epsilon H_0\min \{ |y-z|^2,1\} \), and for a.e. \(y\in U\), simultaneously for all \(z\ne y\),

\[ |\partial _yK_{f,h}(y,z)|+\alpha |K_{f,h}(y,z)|/|y-z| \le C\epsilon H_0\min \{ |y-z|,1\} . \]

Lemma 11.21Cancellation estimate for differentiated blocks

For \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\), noninteger \(\beta {\gt}0\), and every \(m\in \mathbb {N}\), there is \(C_{p,\beta ,m}{\gt}0\) such that for every \(h\in C^\beta (\mathbb {R})\) and \(j\in \mathbb {N}\), \(K_{p,j}*h\) is smooth, its \(m\)th derivative is the absolutely convergent convolution \(K_{p,j}^{(m)}*h\), and

\[ \| \partial ^m(K_{p,j}*h)\| _\infty \le C_{p,\beta ,m}2^{(m-\beta -p)j}N_\beta (h). \]

Lemma 11.19Dyadic block factorization

For \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\), \(v\in C_c^\infty (\mathbb {R};\mathbb {R})\), \(h=|D|^pv\), and every \(j\in \mathbb {N}\),

\[ \Delta _jv(x)=(K_{p,j}*h)(x)\qquad (x\in \mathbb {R}). \]

The convolution and the double integral used in this identity are absolutely convergent.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 11.11Cutoff commutator identity and convergence

Let \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\) and \(w\) be smooth and bounded. Then all integrals in the identity

\[ |D|^p(\eta w)=\eta |D|^pw+C_{\eta ,p}w \]

converge absolutely and the equality holds at every point.

Lemma 11.12Global Holder bound for the commutator

For \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\) and noninteger \(a{\gt}0\) there is \(C_{p,a}{\gt}0\) such that every smooth \(w\in C^a(\mathbb {R})\) satisfies \(C_{\eta ,p}w\in C^a(\mathbb {R})\) and \(N_a(C_{\eta ,p}w)\le C_{p,a}N_a(w)\).

Lemma 11.18Compact-input fractional Fourier bridge

Let \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\) and \(v\in C_c^\infty (\mathbb {R};\mathbb {R})\). The function \(m(\xi )=|\xi |^p\widehat v(\xi )\) is integrable and \(|D|^pv(x)=\check{m}(x)\) pointwise, with absolute convergence on both sides.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 11.25Compact-input global Schauder estimate

Let \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\), \(\beta {\gt}0\), and assume \(\beta \) and \(s=\beta +p\) are nonintegers. There is \(C_{p,\beta }{\gt}0\) such that, for every real \(v\in C_c^\infty (\mathbb {R})\) with \(h=|D|^pv\in C^\beta (\mathbb {R})\),

\[ v\in C^{\beta +p}(\mathbb {R}),\qquad N_{\beta +p}(v)\le C_{p,\beta }\bigl(\| v\| _\infty +N_\beta (h)\bigr). \]

Lemma 11.6Translation differences of the fixed cutoff

For every noninteger \(a{\gt}0\) there is \(C_a{\gt}0\) such that for all \(z\in \mathbb {R}\), \(\eta -\tau _z\eta \in C^a(\mathbb {R})\) and \(N_a(\eta -\tau _z\eta )\le C_a\min \{ |z|,1\} \).

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 11.7Quantitative cutoff extension from the interval

For every noninteger \(a{\gt}0\) there is \(C_a{\gt}0\) such that, for every \(h\in C^a([-1,1])\), the function \(\eta h\), extended by zero outside \([-1,1]\), belongs to \(C^a(\mathbb {R})\) and \(N_a(\eta h)\le C_aN_a(h;[-1,1])\). Values of \(h\) outside \([-1,1]\) have no effect.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 11.2Cutoff and annular-symbol properties

The cutoffs \(\eta ,\chi \) are smooth, real, even and valued in \([0,1]\). The function \(\eta \) equals one on \([-3/4,3/4]\) and has support in \([-7/8,7/8]\); \(\chi \) equals one on \([-1,1]\) and has support in \([-2,2]\). For every \(p\in (0,1)\), \(q_p\) and \(\varphi \) are smooth and supported in \(\{ \xi :1\le |\xi |\le 4\} \). All their derivatives vanish at zero.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 11.24The scalar dyadic increment estimate

For every \(0{\lt}\theta {\lt}1\) there is \(C_\theta {\gt}0\) such that for every \(d\ge 0\) and \(n\in \mathbb {N}\),

\[ \sum _{j=0}^{n-1}\min \{ 2^{-\theta j},d\, 2^{(1-\theta )j}\} \le C_\theta d^\theta . \]

For every \(a{\gt}0\), \(\sum _{j\ge 0}2^{-aj}\) converges, with sum \((1-2^{-a})^{-1}\).

Lemma 11.14Finite dyadic telescoping

For every \(n\in \mathbb {N}\) and \(\xi \in \mathbb {R}\),

\[ \chi (\xi )+\sum _{j=0}^{n-1}\varphi (2^{-j}\xi )=\chi (2^{-n}\xi ). \]

The right side tends to one as \(n\to \infty \) and is bounded in absolute value by one.

Lemma 11.9Far-part smoothness by differentiating the kernel

Let \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\), and let \(w\) be smooth and bounded on \(\mathbb {R}\). Put \(\kappa _p(z)=(1-\chi (z))|z|^{-1-p}\), with value zero near the origin. Every derivative of \(\kappa _p\) is integrable. The far part is

\[ c_p\left(w(x)\int \kappa _p-\int \kappa _p(x-z)w(z)dz\right). \]

It is smooth, and its convolution term can be differentiated any number of times by differentiating \(\kappa _p\). Every such integral converges absolutely, locally uniformly in \(x\).

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 11.10The local right-hand-side norm is finite

For \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\) and smooth bounded \(w\), the singular integral defining \(|D|^pw(x)\) converges absolutely for every \(x\) and is smooth on \(\mathbb {R}\). In particular \(|D|^pw\in C^a([-1,1])\) for every noninteger \(a{\gt}0\). This is a qualitative finiteness assertion; no bound by finitely many global derivatives of \(w\) is assumed or claimed.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 11.8Near-part smoothness without bounds at infinity

Let \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\) and \(w\in C^\infty (\mathbb {R})\), without global derivative bounds. The function \(U(x)=c_p\int \chi (z)(w(x)-w(x-z))|z|^{-1-p}dz\) is smooth. For every \(m\in \mathbb {N}\) its derivative is the same absolutely convergent integral with \(w\) replaced by \(w^{(m)}\). On every compact \(x\) interval all differentiated integrands admit a common integrable majorant, using only the local bound for \(w^{(m+1)}\) on the interval enlarged by two.

Lemma 11.5Integration with a global Holder majorant

Let \(a=k+\theta {\gt}0\), \(k\in \mathbb {N}\), \(0{\lt}\theta {\lt}1\). Let \(F:\mathbb {R}^2\to \mathbb {R}\) and \(B:\mathbb {R}\to [0,\infty )\) be such that \(B\in L^1\), every section \(F(\cdot ,t)\) belongs to \(C^a(\mathbb {R})\), and \(N_a(F(\cdot ,t))\le B(t)\) for every \(t\). Lemma 11.4Global Holder product bound

For every noninteger \(a{\gt}0\) there is \(C_a{\gt}0\) such that for all real \(u,v\in C^a(\mathbb {R})\), \(uv\in C^a(\mathbb {R})\) and \(N_a(uv)\le C_aN_a(u)N_a(v)\).

Lemma 11.3Global Holder translation and restriction

Lemma 11.16Vanishing polynomial moments

For \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\) and all integers \(r,m\ge 0\), the moment integral converges absolutely and

\[ \int _\mathbb {R}z^r K_p^{(m)}(z)dz=0. \]

Lemma 11.17Exact dyadic scaling and weighted norms

For \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\), \(j,m\in \mathbb {N}\), and \(a\ge 0\),

where the symbol at zero is defined to be zero. Moreover,

For \(0{\lt}p{\lt}1\) and noninteger \(\beta {\gt}0\) there is \(C_{p,\beta }{\gt}0\) such that, for smooth \(w\in C^\beta (\mathbb {R})\), \(v=\eta w\) is smooth and compactly supported and \(h=|D|^pv\) belongs to \(C^\beta (\mathbb {R})\) with
