LaTeX Lean
Lemma 11.22Low-frequency bounds from the value norm

For every \(m\in \mathbb {N}\) there is \(C_m{\gt}0\) such that, for every real \(v\in C_c^\infty (\mathbb {R})\), \(S_0v=\chi ^\vee *v\) is smooth and \(\| \partial ^mS_0v\| _\infty \le C_m\| v\| _\infty \). Every differentiated convolution is absolutely convergent.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 11.23Uniform reconstruction, including differentiated partial sums

Let \(v\in C_c^\infty (\mathbb {R};\mathbb {R})\) and \(P_nv=S_0v+\sum _{j=0}^{n-1}\Delta _jv\). For every integer \(m\ge 0\), \(\partial ^mP_nv\to \partial ^mv\) uniformly on \(\mathbb {R}\) as \(n\to \infty \).

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.5Absolute adjoint pairing

For every vector test \(\Phi \), the function \((Y,z)\mapsto K_{\alpha ,c}(z)\cdot (\Phi (Y+z)-\Phi (Y))\) is absolutely integrable on \(E\times E\). The inner integral defining \(B^*\Phi (Y)\) converges absolutely for every \(Y\), and

\[ \| B^*\Phi \| _{L^1(E)}\le C_{\alpha ,c} (\| \Phi \| _{L^1(E)}+\| D\Phi \| _{L^1(E)}). \]

Thus \(\int \theta B^*\Phi \) is absolutely convergent for every bounded measurable \(\theta \).

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.22Bulk-to-contour velocity identity

For a fixed smooth bounded-slope graph, every vector test \(\Phi \) satisfies

\[ \int _E\theta _F(Y)B^*\Phi (Y)dY =-\int _\mathbb {R}A_\Phi (\gamma (s))\cdot \tau (s)ds =\int _E U[F](X)\cdot \Phi (X)dX. \]

All integrals are absolutely convergent. Hence the candidate contour velocity is a locally integrable representative of the independently defined two-dimensional operator \(B_{\alpha ,c}\theta _F\).

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.23Bulk principal values agree with the weak velocity

Set \(u_\varepsilon (X)=\int _{|z|{\gt}\varepsilon }K(z)\theta _F(X-z)dz\) for \(\varepsilon {\gt}0\). Each integral is absolutely convergent. Off the graph, the limit as \(\varepsilon \downarrow 0\) exists and equals the absolutely convergent desingularized integral \(\int K(z)(\theta _F(X-z)-\theta _F(X))dz\). The functions \(u_\varepsilon \) converge in \(L^1_{\rm loc}(E)\) to \(U[F]\); the desingularized expression and \(U[F]\) therefore agree a.e. No boundary vector principal value is asserted.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.17Flux formula for an unbounded subgraph and a compact test field

For a \(C^1\) graph with bounded slope and a compactly supported \(C^1\) vector field \(Q\),

\[ \int _{y{\lt}F(x)}\operatorname {div}Q(X)dX =\int _\mathbb {R}(Q_2-F'Q_1)(x,F(x))dx, \]

with absolute convergence.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.16Finite graph-domain flux formula

Let \(R{\gt}0\), \(F\in C^1(\mathbb {R})\), \(H{\gt}0\) with \(-H{\lt}F(s)\) for \(|s|\le R\), and \(Q:E\to E\) be \(C^1\) on a neighborhood of the closed domain \(D=\{ (s,y):|s|{\lt}R,-H{\lt}y{\lt}F(s)\} \). Then

\[ \begin{split} \int _D\operatorname {div}Q ={}& \int _{-R}^{R}(Q_2-F’Q_1)(s,F(s))ds-\int _{-R}^{R}Q_2(s,-H)ds\\ & +\int _{-H}^{F(R)}Q_1(R,y)dy-\int _{-H}^{F(-R)}Q_1(-R,y)dy . \end{split} \]

Every integral is absolutely convergent.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.26Flat-graph sign and trace check

For \(F=0\) and \(d\ne 0\),

\[ U(x,d)=-c\, C_\alpha |d|^{1-\alpha }(1,0),\qquad C_\alpha =\int _\mathbb {R}(1+s^2)^{-\alpha /2}ds\in (0,\infty ),\qquad W=0. \]

In particular the tangential velocity diverges in magnitude at the boundary while its normal component is zero. Assigning any values to \(U\) on the null graph leaves its weak equations unchanged.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.13Identification with the canonical two-dimensional operator

For every real Schwartz function \(f\) on \(E\), the integral \(B_{\alpha ,c}f(X)=\int K(z)(f(X-z)-f(X))dz\) converges absolutely, belongs to \(L^1(E;E)\), and has Fourier multiplier \(-icA_\alpha J\xi |\xi |^{\alpha -2}\), componentwise. Equivalently, \(B_{\alpha ,c}f=-cA_\alpha \nabla ^\perp (-\Delta )^{-1+\alpha /2}f\). For bounded densities the adjoint pairing and renormalized potential give the same distributional extension.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.9Gamma layer representation of the singular kernel

For \(z\ne 0\),

\[ |z|^{-\alpha }=\frac1{\Gamma (\alpha /2)}\int _0^\infty s^{\alpha /2-1}e^{-s|z|^2}ds,\qquad K_{\alpha ,c}(z)=\frac{2c}{\Gamma (\alpha /2)}Jz\int _0^\infty s^{\alpha /2}e^{-s|z|^2}ds. \]

Both scalar parameter integrals converge absolutely. For each \(\xi \in E\), multiplying the second representation by \(e^{-iz\cdot \xi }-1\) yields an absolutely integrable double integrand in \((s,z)\in (0,\infty )\times E\).

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.10Two-dimensional Gaussian transform and first moment

For every \(s{\gt}0\) and \(\xi \in E\), the following integrals converge absolutely:

\[ \int _Ee^{-s|z|^2-i z\cdot \xi }dz=\frac\pi s e^{-|\xi |^2/(4s)},\qquad \int _E z e^{-s|z|^2-i z\cdot \xi }dz =-\frac{i\pi }{2s^2}\xi e^{-|\xi |^2/(4s)},\qquad \int _E z e^{-s|z|^2}dz=0. \]

The vector formulas are interpreted componentwise after complexification.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.15Measurability, null graphs and a distance bound

Each patch is measurable, each graph has two-dimensional measure zero, and the spacetime graph has three-dimensional measure zero. For a fixed-time slope bound \(|F_x|\le M\), let \(h=s-x\) and \(\delta =y-F(x,t)\). Then

\[ h^2+\delta ^2\le 2(1+M^2)\bigl(h^2+(y-F(s,t))^2\bigr). \]

The same constants work on a compact time interval with its common slope bound.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.11Inverse-parameter Gamma integral

For every \(a,b{\gt}0\), the integrand is integrable on \((0,\infty )\) and

\[ \int _0^\infty s^{-1-a}e^{-b/s}ds=b^{-a}\Gamma (a). \]
LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.12Gaussian evaluation of the velocity symbol

For every \(\xi \in E\), the vector integral is absolutely convergent and

\[ \int _E K_{\alpha ,c}(z)(e^{-iz\cdot \xi }-1)dz =-icA_\alpha J\xi |\xi |^{\alpha -2}, \]

where the right side is zero at \(\xi =0\). In particular \(A_\alpha ,c_{\rm std},\kappa _\alpha {\gt}0\).

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.34Uniform slope for the self-similar family

For every profile supplied by theorem 1.31, the graph \(F_{\epsilon ,T}\) is admissible on \((-\infty ,T)\) and satisfies \(|F_x(x,t)|\le \sqrt\epsilon (C+1)\) for all \(x,t{\lt}T\), with the profile-bound constant \(C\). No global curvature bound is required.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.30Time derivative of the moving-patch pairing

For every scalar spacetime test \(\zeta \),

\[ \int _I\! \int _E\theta _F\partial _t\zeta =-\int _I\! \int _\mathbb {R}F_t(x,t)\zeta (x,F(x,t),t)dxdt, \]

with absolute convergence.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.24Normal-speed convergence and continuity

The integral defining \(W[F](x,t)\) converges absolutely and \(W\) is continuous on \(\mathbb {R}\times I\). For \(|x|\le R\), \(t\in J_0\Subset I\), a bound for the integrand in the variable \(h=s-x\) is

\[ c L_{R,J_0}|h|^{1-\alpha }\mathbf1_{0{\lt}|h|\le 1} +2c M_{J_0}|h|^{-\alpha }\mathbf1_{|h|{\gt}1}, \]

where \(L_{R,J_0}\) bounds \(|F_{xx}|\) on \([-R-1,R+1]\times J_0\).

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.25Two-sided vertical normal trace with an error estimate

For \(d\ne 0\) put \(W_d(x,t)=U_2(x,F(x,t)+d,t)-F_x(x,t)U_1(x,F(x,t)+d,t)\). For every \(R{\gt}0\), \(J_0\Subset I\) there is \(C=C(\alpha ,c,R,J_0,F){\gt}0\) such that

\[ \sup _{|x|\le R,\, t\in J_0}|W_d(x,t)-W(x,t)|\le C|d|^{2-\alpha } \quad (0{\lt}|d|\le 1). \]

Thus both vertical normal traces exist and agree with \(W\).

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.33Local time continuity and the initial-value formulation

For \(R{\gt}0\) and \(s,t\in I\),

\[ \int _{[-R,R]^2}|\theta _F(X,t)-\theta _F(X,s)|dX \le \int _{-R}^R|F(x,t)-F(x,s)|dx. \]

Thus \(t\mapsto \theta _F(t)\) is continuous into \(L^1_{\rm loc}(E)\). If the equivalent equations above hold and \(t_0{\lt}t_1\) both lie in \(I\), let \(\zeta \) be smooth on a neighborhood of \(E\times [t_0,t_1]\), have a common compact spatial support there, and vanish for \(t\) sufficiently close to \(t_1\). It may be nonzero at \(t_0\). Then

\[ \int _{t_0}^{t_1}\! \int _E\theta _F(\partial _t\zeta +U\cdot \nabla \zeta ) +\int _E\theta _F(X,t_0)\zeta (X,t_0)dX=0. \]

For an initial endpoint outside \(I\), this last assertion requires additionally a locally uniform graph limit and a common global slope bound on a one-sided time neighborhood; it is not implied by interior compact-time bounds alone.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.7Absolute convergence of the renormalized potential

For every \(R\ge 1\) there is \(C_{\alpha ,c,R}{\gt}0\) such that for every bounded measurable \(\theta \) with \(|\theta |\le M\), \(M\ge 0\), and every \(|X|\le R\),

\[ \int _E|P(X-Y)-\mathbf1_{|Y|{\gt}1}P(-Y)|\, |\theta (Y)|dY\le C_{\alpha ,c,R}M. \]

The integral defining \(V[\theta ]\) is therefore absolutely convergent at every \(X\), measurable and locally bounded. Changing the subtraction radius to another positive radius changes it by a finite constant independent of \(X\).

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.3Euclidean coordinates and radial majorants

Coordinate identification \(E\leftrightarrow \mathbb {R}\times \mathbb {R}\) preserves Lebesgue measure, and \(|z|^2=z_1^2+z_2^2\). For \(r{\gt}0\),

\[ \int _{|z|{\lt}r}|z|^{-\alpha }dz=\frac{2\pi }{2-\alpha }r^{2-\alpha },\qquad \int _{|z|{\gt}r}|z|^{-\alpha -1}dz=\frac{2\pi }{\alpha -1}r^{1-\alpha }. \]

The displayed nonnegative integrands are integrable on their respective domains. Consequently there is \(C_{\alpha ,c}{\gt}0\) such that for every \(\xi \in E\),

\[ \int _E|K_{\alpha ,c}(z)|\, |e^{-iz\cdot \xi }-1|dz \le C_{\alpha ,c}|\xi |^{\alpha -1}, \]

with the integral zero when \(\xi =0\).

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.8Renormalized potential and its distributional gradient

For every bounded measurable \(\theta \), the defining integral for \(V_{\alpha ,c}[\theta ](X)\) converges absolutely for every \(X\) and defines a locally bounded measurable function. For every vector test \(\Phi \),

\[ \int _E\theta B^*\Phi =-\int _E V_{\alpha ,c}[\theta ]\, \operatorname {div}(J\Phi ). \]

Both sides converge absolutely. This is \(B_{\alpha ,c}\theta =-J\nabla V_{\alpha ,c}[\theta ]\) in distributions. Replacing the subtraction radius \(1\) by another positive radius changes \(V\) by a finite constant independent of \(X\) and leaves the velocity unchanged.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.29Spatial weak flux across the actual graph

For every fixed \(t\in I\) and scalar spatial test \(\zeta \),

\[ \int _{\Omega _t}U(X,t)\cdot \nabla \zeta (X)dX =\int _\mathbb {R}W(x,t)\zeta (x,F(x,t))dx. \]

Both integrals are absolutely convergent, with estimates uniform on compact time intervals for tests with a common compact support and bounded first derivatives.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.6Test potential and adjoint divergence identity

For a vector test \(\Phi \), let \(A_\Phi (Y)=\int _E P_{\alpha ,c}(X-Y)\Phi (X)dX\). This integral is absolutely convergent, \(A_\Phi \) is \(C^1\), and

\[ B^*\Phi =-\operatorname {div}(J A_\Phi ). \]

If \(\operatorname {supp}\Phi \subset \{ |X|\le L\} \), then for \(|Y|{\gt}2L+1\), \(|A_\Phi (Y)|\le C_{\alpha ,c}|Y|^{-\alpha }\| \Phi \| _1\). In particular \(B^*(\nabla \zeta )=0\) for every scalar test \(\zeta \).

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.4\(L^1\) translation estimate for test fields

For every vector test function \(\Phi :E\to E\) and every \(z\in E\),

\[ \int _E|\Phi (Y+z)-\Phi (Y)|dY \le \min \left(|z|\int _E\| D\Phi (Y)\| dY,\ 2\int _E|\Phi (Y)|dY\right). \]

All the displayed integrals are finite.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.35Exact time normalization

Let \(p=\alpha -1\), \(\kappa =\kappa _\alpha {\gt}0\) and let an admissible \(F\) solve the normalized front equation on \(I\). Then \(G(x,t)=F(x,t/\kappa )\), on \(\{ t:t/\kappa \in I\} \), is admissible and satisfies the coefficient-\(c_{\rm std}\) graph equation. If \(I=(-\infty ,T/\kappa )\), the new interval is \((-\infty ,T)\). For the self-similar ansatz its physical scale is

\[ L_{\rm std}(t)=(\alpha (T-t)/\kappa )^{1/\alpha }. \]
LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.31Lifting tests from the graph

For every scalar test \(\psi \in C_c^\infty (\mathbb {R}\times I)\) there is a scalar spacetime test \(\zeta \in C_c^\infty (E\times I)\) satisfying \(\zeta (x,F(x,t),t)=\psi (x,t)\). Consequently a continuous \(r:\mathbb {R}\times I\to \mathbb {R}\) whose integral against all these traces is zero must vanish pointwise.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.21Artificial-boundary errors vanish

Fix a time and \(|F'|\le M\). Put \(H_R=|F(0)|+(M+1)R+1\) and \(D_R=\{ |x|{\lt}R,-H_R{\lt}y{\lt}F(x)\} \). For every vector test \(\Phi \), the sum of the three artificial-boundary contributions in the finite graph flux formula for \(Q=J A_\Phi \) has modulus at most \(C_{\alpha ,c,M,F(0),\Phi }R^{1-\alpha }\) for all sufficiently large \(R\). The constant and lower threshold for \(R\) are chosen independently of \(R\).

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.18Off-graph velocity convergence and size

For \(|F_x|\le M\) the contour integral for \(U(X,t)\) converges absolutely at every \(X\notin \Gamma _t\). There is \(C_{\alpha ,c,M}{\gt}0\), independent of \(F,X\), such that

\[ |U((x,y),t)|\le C_{\alpha ,c,M}|y-F(x,t)|^{1-\alpha }\quad (y\ne F(x,t)). \]
LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.20Spatial smoothness and divergence-free velocity

For each fixed time, \(U\) is spatially \(C^1\) on \(E\setminus \Gamma _t\) and \(\operatorname {div}_X U=0\) there. Its first spatial derivatives are jointly continuous in \((X,t)\) off the spacetime graph. No time differentiability of \(U\) is claimed from the present hypotheses.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.28Spacetime velocity law and uniqueness of the representative

For every admissible \(F\), the representative \(U[F]\) satisfies the coefficient-\(c\) velocity law on \(E\times I\). Every other locally integrable velocity satisfying that law for \(\theta _F\) equals \(U[F]\) a.e. in spacetime. Such velocities are divergence-free distributionally in space.

LaTeX Lean
Lemma 12.19Local integrability and joint contour-test Fubini

For an admissible graph, \(U\) is jointly measurable and locally integrable on \(E\times I\). For a compact spatial set \(Q\) and compact time interval \(J_0\subset I\), \(\int _{J_0}\int _Q|U|{\lt}\infty \). For every compactly supported spatial test \(\Phi \), the integrand \(|\tau _t(s)||X-\gamma _t(s)|^{-\alpha }|\Phi (X)|\) is integrable in \((s,X)\); its bound is uniform in \(t\in J_0\) for tests supported in a fixed compact set with bounded sup norm.

There are \(\epsilon _c{\gt}0\) (depending only on \(p,\chi _+\) and the constant \(C_0\) of lemma 3.12) and, for every admissible \(\gamma \), a constant \(C(\gamma )\) such that for all \(0\le \epsilon \le \epsilon _c\):

Let \(\epsilon _0,\delta ,\overline{B}\) be as in theorem 2.20, where \(\epsilon _0\le \epsilon _c\) with \(\epsilon _c\) the threshold of lemma 8.25. Then:

Lemma 9.30Symbol bounds

For every \(L\ge 0\), \(k\ge 0\) there are constants \(C_L\), \(C_{k,L}\) (depending on \(p,\chi \)) such that for all \(y\in \mathbb {R}\) and \(R\ge R_0(y)\):

  1. \(k=0\): paper eq. eqn:linear_nonstationary_leading_kernel_j0, i.e. \(|\operatorname {Re}\partial _z\check{m^R_{0,0}(y,\cdot )}(z)|\le C_L\langle y \rangle ^{-1}\langle z \rangle ^{-L}\), and (paper eq. eqn:linear_nonstationary_leading_kernel_j12) for \(z\neq 0\), \(|\operatorname {Re}\partial _z\check{m^R_{1,0}(y,\cdot )}(z)|+|\operatorname {Re}\check{m^R_{2,0}(y,\cdot )}(z)|\) is bounded by \(2C_L\) times the three-region function of lemma 9.25;

Lemma 9.32Remainder kernel

For \(M\ge 2\) there is \(C_M\) (depending on \(p,\chi ,M\)) such that for all \(R\ge 2\), \(j\in \{ 0,1,2\} \), \(y,z\in \mathbb {R}\): \(|K^R_{\mathcal{R}_{j,M}}(y,z)|\le C_M\langle y \rangle ^{-M}w_E(z)\), i.e. \(\lesssim _M\langle y \rangle ^{-M}\langle z \rangle ^{-1}\) for \(z\le 0\) and \(\lesssim _M\langle y \rangle ^{-M}\langle z \rangle ^{\frac{1-p}{2p}}\) for \(z{\gt}0\).

\[ m_{j,0}^R(y,\xi ):=\frac{a_j^{\textup{ns},R}(y,\xi )}{i(y-\xi ^p)},\qquad m_{j,k+1}^R(y,\xi ):=-\frac{\partial _\xi m_{j,k}^R(y,\xi )}{i(y-\xi ^p)}, \]

(paper eq. eqn:linear_nonstationary_expansion) for admissible \(\gamma \) and \(G\in \widetilde{Y}_\gamma \), \(\mathcal{T}_{+,j}^{\textup{ns},R}G(y)=2\pi \sum _{k=0}^{M-1}\bigl[\check{m_{j,k}^R(y,\cdot )}*G'\bigr](y)+\mathcal{R}_{j,M}^RG(y)\) with \(\mathcal{R}^R_{j,M}G(y):=\int K^R_{\mathcal{R}_{j,M}}(y,z)G'(z)dz\) (paper eq. eqn:linear_nonstationary_remainder_definition); all integrals absolutely convergent.

Lemma 3.46Van der Corput, paper form

Lemma 3.7Kernel bounds; Remark “vanishing diagonal”

Let \(1{\lt}\alpha {\lt}2\) and \(R\ge 1\). There are constants \(C_j=C(j,R,\alpha )\) such that for all \(0\le \epsilon \le 1\) and all \(|u|,|v|\le R\):

  1. \(|\widetilde{\Gamma }_\epsilon (u,v)|\le C_0\epsilon (|u|+|v|)\) and \(|\nabla ^j\widetilde{\Gamma }_\epsilon (u,v)|\le C_j\epsilon \) for all \(j\ge 0\);

Theorem 12.32Two-dimensional patch equation is equivalent to the graph equation

Let \(F\) be admissible. Then \((\theta _F,U_{\alpha ,c}[F])\) solves the coefficient-\(c\) weak patch system if and only if

\[ F_t(x,t)=c\int _\mathbb {R}\frac{F_x(x,t)-F_x(s,t)}{((x-s)^2+(F(x,t)-F(s,t))^2)^{\alpha /2}}ds \quad (x\in \mathbb {R},t\in I). \]

The same equivalence holds with any locally integrable \(u\) satisfying the velocity law, interpreted up to a.e. equality. Every front integral is absolutely convergent.

Theorem 12.36Canonical two-dimensional patches forming a corner

Let \(\alpha \in (7/4,2)\) and \(p=\alpha -1\). There exist \(\epsilon _0,C{\gt}0\), depending only on \(\alpha \), such that for every \(0{\lt}\epsilon {\lt}\epsilon _0\) there is a profile \(f_\epsilon \) satisfying all profile estimates of theorem 1.31 with constant \(C\) and the following property. For every \(T{\gt}0\), define

\[ G(x,t)=\sqrt\epsilon L_{\rm std}(t)f_\epsilon (x/L_{\rm std}(t)),\qquad \theta (X,t)=\mathbf1_{X_2{\lt}G(X_1,t)},\qquad u=U_{\alpha ,c_{\rm std}}[G]. \]

Then on \(E\times (-\infty ,T)\) the pair is a weak solution of

\[ \partial _t\theta +\operatorname {div}(\theta u)=0,\qquad u=-\nabla ^\perp (-\Delta )^{-1+\alpha /2}\theta , \]

with the canonical normalization defined above and with the initial trace at \(t=0\). The interface is smooth for \(t{\lt}T\) and \(\| G(\cdot ,t)-\sqrt\epsilon x_-\| _\infty \le C\sqrt\epsilon (T-t)^{1/\alpha }\). For each such \(\epsilon \) there is \(b_\epsilon {\gt}0\), independent of \(T\) and \(\delta \), such that for every \(T,\delta {\gt}0\) there is \(t_\delta {\lt}T\) with \(\sup _{|x|{\lt}\delta }|\partial _x^2G(x,t)|\ge b_\epsilon (T-t)^{-1/\alpha }\) whenever \(t_\delta {\lt}t{\lt}T\). Moreover, with \(\theta _*(X)=\mathbf1_{X_2{\lt}\sqrt\epsilon (X_1)_-}\), \(\theta (t)\to \theta _*\) in \(L^1_{\rm loc}(E)\) as \(t\uparrow T\). This is an infinite-area patch result; no global \(L^1\) assumption on \(\theta \) is made.
